# Module 08 Strategy Schema

## Strategy-to-action starter plans

Apply `FW_41`. Keep the existing strategy fields and schema version; attach the separately versioned `strategy-to-action: 1.0` transport defined in `templates/strategy-to-action/plan.schema.json` through `starter-plan-refs` in the handoff/private manifest. A plan references existing decision, consequence and evidence records; ownership of those strategy fields stays with their source. Derive the recommended Starter Plan after source acceptance. Human adoption, production and release are separate decisions. Do not silently rewrite or automatically reapprove a previously locked strategy.

## FW_32 source-owned accountability records

The internal canonical state adds `material_decisions`, `assumptions`, `implementation_consequences`, `cost_drivers` and `decision_measurement_contracts` using the exact schemas in `framework/FW_32-Strategy-Accountability-Implementation-and-Decision-Support-Contract.md`. Client views may explain selected effects and implementation implications but do not expose raw governance schemas.

For each material decision, record at least one intended effect and a named rule for the next decision. Record each material implication for evidence, assets or publishing as a consequence. Give every estimable work unit a Cost Driver without a monetary rate. Keep evidence strength, content depth and publication state separate.

## Editorial read-contract — required

Include every editorial field in `FW_27`. Distinguish existing evidence from evidence still required, and include a concrete walkthrough from the first source to a decision. Give each planned piece one reader question and one evidence class. Keep publication permission separate, and place qualifications beside the claims they limit. Treat book material as a governed source; do not simply reproduce chapters. Keep traces of the method internal.

Structural checks may pass the language, framework-purpose, redundancy, terminology and qualification fields. Cold-reader comprehension remains `pending` until tested.

## Governed strategy outputs

The client-readable canonical authority and full strategy is `08-content-strategy.md`. When routed, emit `08-content-strategy-executive-view.md`, `08-content-strategy-presentation-view.md`, `08-content-strategy-strategic-snapshot.md` and, where production follows, `08-content-strategy-practitioner-brief.md`. The brief uses schema `1.2`, `view-version: 3.0.0`, `format: Langfell-hybrid-practitioner-brief`, the common V3 spine and the Proof-and-Content-specific middle. Views and the brief inherit the canonical states and lock ID, and consume the canonical file plus transient view-source state. The former Comprehensive View is superseded by the canonical strategy.

**This contract defines the locked structure that downstream skills read.** Every downstream skill uses it to locate information in the M08 proof-strategy document. `08_13-Content-Handoff-Pack.md` defines *which* outputs carry downstream and *why*; this document defines *exactly where each one lives* so a skill can locate it reliably.

The Handoff Pack explains the outputs; this schema specifies their structure. It is the M08 equivalent of `05`/`06`/`07-Strategy-Schema.md` and follows the same conventions (numbered read-keys, token-match read-rule, alias map, graceful degradation).

**Schema version: 1.4.** Pin this in `dmode.config.md` (`m08-strategy: 1.4`). Skills declare the schema version they were built against; a mismatch is a compatibility check, not a silent failure.

> **What's load-bearing here is different.** M06/M07 are statement-based; M08 is **pillar + proof**. The source library a content skill adapts is the **Content Pillars** (`08_02`), and the evidence it deploys is the **Proof Hierarchy** (`08_03`). There is no fixed statement count — pillars are a variable-length list keyed `Pillar N`.

> **Audience note (why numbered headings).** `08-content-strategy.md` is the complete client working strategy and a stable read surface for skills. Each deliverable is keyed to its sub-module number (`08_NN`). Use plain descriptive labels with those keys so the client never has to decode the framework.

---

## Client output wrapper — required

Before `08_00`, emit the seven-part canonical opening in `FW_26`. Explain what proof exists, what is missing, which buyer doubts take priority and which assets come first. State which claims are allowed or prohibited, and distinguish fixed, flexible and unresolved decisions. Explain what the evidence permits before introducing internal proof-class labels. The client body must not contain internal controls; those remain in `08_13-Content-Handoff-Pack.md` or the manifest. `08_08` defines proof sequence; Module 11 owns publishing quantities and cadence.

Required client-file metadata fields: `document-state`, `client-decision-state`, `evidence-state`, `source-authority-state`, `production-state`. Legacy status fields are prohibited in client-rendered files. Richer lifecycle states remain in the Handoff Pack or internal run manifest. Proof-gap run state must be reconciled with the current run manifest.

## Consultancy Decision Record — internal handoff only

Canonical fields: `decision_id`, `module`, `decision_area`, `situation`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_status`, `confidence`, `diagnosis`, `options_considered`, `comparison_criteria`, `recommendation`, `rationale`, `accepted_trade_off`, `client_decision`, `conditions`, `owner`, `review_event`, `progression_condition`, `invalidation_triggers`, `downstream_authority`.


The client narrative performs the seven consultancy functions in `FW_25`. Store the machine record only in `08_13-Content-Handoff-Pack.md` with the full `Consultancy Decision Record`, plus `urgent_proof_gap`, `first_evidence`, `recommended_formats`, `publication_exclusions`, `evidence_needed_objections`, `premature_production` and `decision_closing_event`.

## Canonical output

**File:** `clients/[brand]/output/08-content-strategy.md` (one file per client). *(Flat path for v1.x; revisit if a `strategy/` subfolder is adopted in `dmode.config.md`.)*

**Heading convention:** `## 08_NN [Name]` for each deliverable; pillars addressed `Pillar N` within `08_02`; proof tiers by tier name within `08_03`. `###`/`####` = field within a deliverable. Imported brand + upstream layer sits in `## 08_00`.

```text
# Module 08: Proof Strategy — [Brand Name]
<frontmatter: schema: m08-strategy · schema-version: 1.4 · brand · archetype>

## 08_00 Brand + Upstream Layer (imported)
### RouteAuthorization          route, status, capability_profile, authorised_human_decision, decision_owner, closure_conditions, permitted_channels, permitted_offers, permitted_audiences, generation_permission (M04 04-Handoff-Pack)
### Belief Shift Journey        FROM / TO            (M05 05_03)
### Brand Voice                                      (M05 05_07)
### Copywriting Rules                                (M05 05_12)
### Claims Boundaries           Can / Must Qualify / Cannot   (M05 05_00, locked deployment Claims Boundaries)
### Marketing Statements        S1–S10               (M06)
### Sales Objections            Top 10               (M07 07_04)

## 08_01 Brand-Grounded Content Summary
## 08_02 Brand-Derived Pillars                  ← ANCHOR (the content source library)
### Pillar 1 [Name]            + "What This Pillar Proves"
### Pillar 2 [Name]            …
### Pillar N [Name]            (variable count)
### Public Specialisation Signal at least one pillar; what / for whom / problem / distinctive perspective or method; no unsupported exclusivity
## 08_03 Proof Hierarchy                        ← ANCHOR (what evidence to deploy)
### Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3   (foundation → expand → scale)
### Tier 1 Citation Readiness  referenceability / evidence / method / independent usefulness / limits / Claims Boundary; not an evidence upgrade
## 08_04 Proof Gap Analysis
### VOC Calibration            calibrated / evidence-pending / not-applicable; expression change; strategic-fidelity check
### Decision-Infrastructure View existing proof / weak or absent proof / unresolved objections / priority assets / client-facing state
## 08_05 Content-to-Objection Map               ← ANCHOR (which pillar answers which objection; include reverse mapping from proof gap to planned content)
## 08_06 Claims Boundaries for Content          ← ANCHOR (claims governance for this module; explicit separation of evidence claim vs content claim)
## 08_07 Proof Distribution Channels
## 08_08 Proof Production Priorities
## 08_09 Proof Metrics & Transfer Indicators
### Qualitative Belief-Transfer Sources conversations / questions / comments / replies / calls / objections / customer language; engagement alone insufficient
## 08_10 Production Process
## 08_11 Resources & Constraints
## 08_12 Claims Compliance Review
## 08_13 Content Handoff Pack                INTERNAL ONLY — emit to 08_13-Content-Handoff-Pack.md, not the client body
### Publication state table per content piece: release_class, required_review, checks_completed, permission_event, reviewer_role, publication_state
### Source capture and expiry for each proof asset
### Trace to Module 03 proof commitments (optional but recommended)
```

---

## The load-bearing fields

| What | Read-key | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Content Pillars** (variable list, each with "What This Pillar Proves") | `08_02 → Pillar N` | The source library — every content piece adapts one (or a defined few) pillar(s) |
| **Proof Hierarchy** (tiered) | `08_03 → Tier N` | The evidence a piece is allowed to deploy, strongest-available-first |
| **Content-to-Objection Map** | `08_05` | Which pillar answers which M07 objection — drives piece purpose |
| **Claims Boundaries for Content** | `08_06` | Module-level claims governance (cross-checks M05) |

**For schema validation:** `08_02` (Pillars) and `08_03` (Proof Hierarchy) **must be present and non-empty**. At least one pillar carries the Public Specialisation Signal. Every relevant Tier 1 asset carries Citation Readiness without upgrading its evidence state. `08_04` is required before substantive 08B generation and records VOC as `calibrated`, `evidence-pending` or `not-applicable`; missing VOC cannot be fabricated or used to rewrite strategy. `08_05` and `08_06` are anchor-grade. Belief-transfer measurement must name qualitative evidence sources when available and cannot pass on engagement alone. Module 08 may define sequence and readiness; Module 11 owns quantities, cadence and dates.

The imported **Belief Shift Journey** (`08_00`, from M05 `05_03`) is required. All proof must serve that journey.

---

## Read-contract for skills

1. **Locate deliverables by sub-module number, pillars by pillar number.** `## 08_NN`; `Pillar N` within `08_02`. The number is invariant; the label may be reworded.
2. **Numbered keys are canonical.** `08_03` not "the proof section"; `08_02 → Pillar 3` not "the third theme".
3. **Read the derived value, not the scaffolding.** The emitter wraps each deliverable in the FW_16 two-step structure (`### Upstream Anchors (verbatim — Step 1)` → `#### [Name] (derived from above — Step 2)` → Traceability). Read the **Step 2 / derived** block. If absent (clean output), read the section body.
4. **Tolerate aliases during transition** — resolve via the Alias Map.
5. **Pillars + Proof Hierarchy guaranteed, the rest optional.** `08_02`, `08_03`, plus `08_05`/`08_06`, guaranteed; degrade gracefully elsewhere.
6. **Proof discipline.** A content piece deploys the **strongest available** proof tier for its job and never claims proof not present in `08_03`. If a piece needs proof the hierarchy doesn't have, that's a Proof Gap (`08_04`) — surface it, don't fabricate.
7. **Version-check** the frontmatter `schema-version` against the skill's declared version.

**Cross-module read.** `08_00` holds imported copies for convenience. Read authoritative brand fields from M05 (`05-Strategy-Schema.md`), marketing statements from M06 (`06-Strategy-Schema.md`) and objection language from M07 (`07-Strategy-Schema.md`, `07_04`). A content piece requires all four modules.

**Scripture / textual claims (conditional).** When a content piece makes scriptural, historical, or other externally-verifiable textual claims (faith-based content, the books), the `os-content-piece` skill invokes `book-scripture-check` before declaring done. Not applicable to ordinary business clients (e.g. Langfell itself) — the integration is conditional on the content's subject, not always-on.

---

## Alias Map (current emission → canonical)

The client output (`clients/Langfell/output/08-content-strategy.md`) already heads deliverables with the `08_NN` token (`### Deliverable 08_NN: [Name]`) and pillars `**Pillar N: [Name]**`. The emitter (`08-Prompt.md`) heads deliverables `### 08_NN [Name]`.

**Read-rule (robust): match the `08_NN` token (deliverable) or `Pillar N` (pillar), not an exact heading string.** Find the token in the heading hierarchy, then read its Step-2 block or section body.

| Current heading | Read-key |
| --- | --- |
| `### Deliverable 08_NN: [Name]` (client file) | `08_NN` (token in heading) |
| `### 08_NN [Name]` (emitter) | `08_NN` |
| `**Pillar N: [Name]**` → "What This Pillar Proves" | `08_02 → Pillar N` |
| Tier headings within Proof Hierarchy (`Tier 1/2/3`) | `08_03 → Tier N` |
| `## Phase 1 / 2 …` groupings | dropped — deliverables stand on their own |

---

## Migration status

- [x] **Schema locked** (v1.1) — this document.
- [x] **Skills can read current output** — the `08_NN` + `Pillar N` token-match read-rule resolves both the client file and the emitter without a prompt-file change. The client file already carries `08_NN` tokens, so deliverable reads are direct.
- [ ] **Cosmetic emitter reformat (optional, non-blocking)** — opportunistic on the next real M08 run.
- [ ] **Final roll-out module** — apply the same lock to M10 (M05, M06, M07, M08 now done; M09 uses os-page-brief/os-page-copy).

---

## Validation: content-piece (the new consumer)

`.claude/skills/content-piece/SKILL.md` reads M08 against this schema. All reads resolve against `clients/Langfell/output/08-content-strategy.md`:

| content-piece input | Read-key |
| --- | --- |
| Content Pillars (the source library) | `08_02 → Pillar N` |
| Proof Hierarchy (evidence to deploy) | `08_03 → Tier N` |
| Content-to-Objection Map (piece purpose) | `08_05` |
| Claims Boundaries for Content | `08_06` |
| Proof Gaps (don't fabricate past these) | `08_04` |
| Belief Shift Journey (the spine) | `08_00 → ### Belief Shift Journey` (M05 `05_03`) |
| Marketing statements / sales objections (consistency) | M06 `S1`–`S10` / M07 `07_04` |

Brand-layer reads (Voice, Copywriting rules, Claims Boundaries, Core Values) resolve against `05-Strategy-Schema.md`.

---

## Version History

- Added visible specialisation, Tier 1 Citation Readiness, VOC calibration, decision-infrastructure proof gaps and qualitative belief-transfer evidence to their canonical sections.
- Kept referenceability separate from evidence strength and customer language subordinate to approved strategy.

| Version | Date | Changes |

| 1.0 | 2026-06-01 | Initial M08 schema lock. Pillar + proof model (not statement-based): `08_02` Content Pillars (variable `Pillar N` list) and `08_03` Proof Hierarchy (tiered) as the guaranteed load-bearing fields; `08_05` Content-to-Objection Map + `08_06` Claims Boundaries anchor-grade. `08_NN` / `Pillar N` token-match read-rule; Step-2-derived read discipline; proof-tier discipline (strongest available, never fabricate past `08_04`); conditional `scripture-check` integration note; Alias Map for the client file (already `08_NN`-tagged) and emitter; validated against the content-piece skill and the Langfell client file. Mirrors `07-Strategy-Schema.md`. |

# Module 08B Content Generator

> **Client paths:** Before reading inputs or writing outputs, resolve the selected client using `../templates/00-Entry-Brief-Folder-Convention.md`. Its Input, Output, collection, asset and private run destinations override legacy flat output examples. Keep existing authority and approval gates unchanged.


## Current runtime contract — governing

Use this file as an optional reference for content formats and the use of proof. `os-communication-router` checks authority and selects behaviour C, E or C+E in a valid packet. `.agents/skills/os-content-piece/SKILL.md` writes from that packet, consulting the relevant content-type guidance here when needed. Specialist checks, claims validation and editing are separate passes.

Later instructions to gather Module 04–08 sources directly, use one universal structure, show derivation or run every diagnostic while drafting remain as manual reference material. They do not govern the current runtime.

## Initiative Authority Gate

Production requires a current, accepted Initiative Authority Record. It must contain the initiative ID/version, Direction ID/version and strategic move ID, plus the authorised audience/trigger, movement, offer, proof, channel, claims, exclusions, success and invalidation fields. Return `authority-input-incomplete` if authority is missing, incomplete, stale or does not permit the requested work. Record all three authority IDs on the output. If that authority is invalidated, the asset becomes stale.

**Langfell™**
_The content rules library — content-type guidelines, generation process, proof discipline_

---

## How the os-content-piece skill uses this file

`.agents/skills/os-content-piece/SKILL.md` is the per-piece runtime; this file is an optional reference it may consult selectively.

| Layer | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| **Rules / logic library** | **this file** | Content-type guidelines, generation process, output format, proof-deployment + claims discipline, quality gate. Updated centrally. |
| **Per-piece runtime** | `os-content-piece/SKILL.md` | Inputs, pillar selection, proof planning, generation, storage, cross-piece coherence, conditional scripture-check, re-run logic. Calls these rules. |
| **Cross-piece context** | `RUN_ROOT/content/_cross-piece-context.md` | Prevents overuse of one proof asset or opening, and repeated coverage of a pillar already supported by sufficient proof. |

**Don't duplicate rules into the skill.** Change a content-type guideline or proof rule here; the skill reads it. The skill reads M08 against `08-Strategy-Schema.md` (pillars `08_02 → Pillar N`; proof hierarchy `08_03`; objection map `08_05`), M05 brand layer against `05-Strategy-Schema.md`, and M06/M07 for consistency.

**Stay in long-form:** short broadcast assets are `os-marketing-asset` (06B); sales assets are `os-sales-asset` (07B); pages are `os-page-copy` (09B). This library is long-form proof-bearing content only. When content makes scriptural/textual claims, the skill runs `book-scripture-check`.

---

## Overview

Module 08B generates actual content pieces from the strategy defined in Module 08. Module 08 answers "what content should we create and why?" Module 08B answers "write this specific piece."

This separates strategy decisions from content production as needed, following the pattern used by 06B, 07B and 09B.

---

## When to Use This Module

Use Module 08B when you have:

- Completed Module 08 (Content Pillars, Proof Hierarchy defined)
- Module 05 Voice (`05_07`) and Copywriting rules (`05_12`) available
- Approved RouteAuthorization from Module 04
- A specific content piece to generate

Do NOT use if:

- Module 08 is incomplete (no pillars defined)
- Module 05 Voice or Copywriting rules are missing
- Module 04 RouteAuthorization `status` is not `Approved` or `Overridden`, or `generation_permission` is `draft-only`, and the requested piece would be public or buyer-facing
- You don't know which pillar the content serves

---

## Required Inputs

Before generating content, gather these from completed modules:

### From Module 04 (RouteAuthorization)

```text
ROUTEAUTHORIZATION:
- route: [name]
- status: [Approved / Draft / Overridden / etc.]
- capability_profile: [full / reduced]
- authorised_human_decision: [verbatim]
- decision_owner: [name + role]
- closure_conditions: [text]
- permitted_channels: [list]
- permitted_offers: [list]
- permitted_audiences: [list]
- generation_permission: [draft-only / publish-ready]
```

Do not generate publishable content for a route, audience, proof path, or offer not listed in `permitted_*`. If `generation_permission` is `draft-only`, output draft-only internal options. If `status` is not `Approved` or `Overridden`, halt and request route approval.

### From Module 08 (Proof Strategy)

```text
CONTENT PILLARS (from 08_02):

Pillar 1: [Brand-Specific Name]

- Type: [Disruption / Vision / Method / Evidence / Defence]
- What it proves: [Connection to Brand Strategy]
- Belief Stage: [Recognition / Disruption / Alternative / Proof / Adoption]

Pillar 2: [Brand-Specific Name]
[Same structure]

Pillar 3: [Brand-Specific Name]
[Same structure]

[Continue for 3-5 pillars]
```
```text
PROOF HIERARCHY (from 08_03):

Tier 1 (Foundation):

- Definition: [What qualifies]
- Depth: Comprehensive, authoritative
- Examples: Pillar pages, guides, research, detailed case studies

Tier 2 (Supporting):

- Definition: [What qualifies]
- Depth: Focused, practical
- Examples: Blog posts, how-tos, specific case studies

Tier 3 (Distribution):

- Definition: [What qualifies]
- Depth: Accessible, scannable
- Examples: Social posts, newsletter snippets, short videos
```
### From Module 05 (Brand Identity)

```text
BRAND VOICE:

- Tone: [Characteristics]
- Do: [Voice guidelines]
- Don't: [Anti-patterns]

COPYWRITING FRAMEWORK:
[The framework from Module 05]

BELIEF SHIFT:

- FROM: [Limiting belief]
- TO: [Empowering belief]

CLAIMS BOUNDARIES:

- Can Claim: [List]
- Must Qualify: [List]
- Cannot Claim: [List]
```
### From Module 01 (Natural Language Bank)

```text
NATURAL LANGUAGE BANK:
[Paste the Natural Language Bank from Module 01 Handoff Pack]
```
Use the builder’s vocabulary, energy patterns and natural language captured in Module 01 to preserve their voice in the content.

---

## Content Request Format

When requesting content, specify:

```text
CONTENT REQUEST:

Content Type: [Blog post / Article / Case study / Guide / etc.]
Pillar: [Which pillar this serves]
Tier: [1 / 2 / 3]
Working Title: [Suggested title]
Target Length: [Word count or "standard for tier"]
Specific Focus: [What aspect of the pillar to address]
Objection Addressed: [If applicable, from 08_05]
Call to Action: [What reader should do next]
```

---

## Generator Prompt

### Identity & Purpose

You generate content that proves the brand's belief. Every piece you produce must:

- Serve a specific Content Pillar (from Module 08)
- Meet Tier requirements (depth, authority, format)
- Follow Module 05 Voice and Copywriting rules
- Stay within Claims Boundaries
- Move the reader along the Belief Shift

### Core Principle

**Content is Proof, Not Promotion**

Show, explain or support the brand’s belief with evidence. An assertion alone is insufficient.

### Content Type Guidelines

#### Blog Posts (Tier 2)

**Purpose:** Focused exploration of one aspect of a pillar
**Length:** 800-1,500 words
**Structure:**

- Hook that connects to reader's current belief
- Problem/tension that the pillar addresses
- Insight or method that proves the brand's position
- Practical takeaway or application
- Connection to foundation proof (Tier 1)

**Voice:** Conversational but authoritative. First person plural ("we") when representing brand perspective.

---

#### Long-Form Articles (Tier 1)

**Purpose:** Comprehensive, definitive treatment of a pillar topic
**Length:** 2,000-4,000 words
**Structure:**

- Executive summary / key takeaways
- Context: Why this matters now
- The problem: Current belief and its costs
- The alternative: Brand's position with evidence
- The method: How to apply this thinking
- Proof points: Cases, data, examples
- Implications: What this means going forward
- Call to action

**Voice:** Authoritative, well-researched. Can include data, quotes, examples.

---

#### Case Studies (Tier 1 or 2)

**Purpose:** Third-party validation of brand's belief
**Length:** 1,000-2,000 words (Tier 1) or 500-800 words (Tier 2)
**Structure:**

- Situation: Client's starting point (aligned with "FROM" belief)
- Challenge: What they were struggling with
- Approach: How brand's method was applied
- Results: What changed (quantified where possible)
- Reflection: Client's perspective shift (aligned with "TO" belief)

**Voice:** Narrative, specific. Let the client's experience tell the story.

**Claims Check:** All results must be within "Can Claim" boundaries. Qualify anything in "Must Qualify."

---

#### Thought Leadership (Tier 1)

**Purpose:** Establish brand as authority on the pillar topic
**Length:** 1,500-2,500 words
**Structure:**

- Provocative opening: Challenge conventional wisdom
- The observation: What you've noticed that others miss
- The argument: Why your perspective is more accurate
- The evidence: Support from experience, data, examples
- The implication: What this means for the reader
- The invitation: How to engage further

**Voice:** Confident, distinctive. This is where brand personality shows most.

---

#### How-To Guides (Tier 2)

**Purpose:** Practical application of brand's method
**Length:** 1,000-2,000 words
**Structure:**

- What you'll learn (outcome)
- Why this approach (brief connection to brand belief)
- Prerequisites / what you need
- Step-by-step process
- Common mistakes to avoid
- What success looks like
- Next steps / deeper resources

**Voice:** Instructional, clear. Focus on reader's success.

---

#### Newsletter Content (Tier 3)

**Purpose:** Maintain connection, drive to proof library
**Length:** 300-600 words
**Structure:**

- One insight or observation
- Brief exploration
- Link to deeper content (Tier 1 or 2)
- Personal note / human element

**Voice:** Personal, conversational. As if writing to someone you respect.

---

#### Social Thought Leadership (Tier 3)

**Purpose:** Distribute ideas, drive traffic to proof
**Length:** 80–300 words (or platform-appropriate)
**Structure:**

- Hook (first line must stop scroll)
- One clear point
- Brief support
- Engagement prompt or link to more

**Voice:** Punchy, memorable. Adapted to platform norms while maintaining brand voice.

---

### Generation Process

**Step 1: Confirm Inputs**

- Which pillar does this serve?
- What tier is this content?
- What Belief Shift stage does it address?

**Step 2: Apply Voice + Copywriting Rules**
Import Module 05 Voice and Copywriting rules and apply them to this piece.

**Step 3: Draft Content**
Write the content following the type-specific guidelines above.

**Step 4: Claims Check**
Review every claim against Claims Boundaries:

- Can Claim: State directly
- Must Qualify: Add softening language
- Cannot Claim: Remove or reframe

**Step 5: Voice Check**
Does this sound like the brand (per Module 05 Brand Voice)?

**Step 6: Proof Check**
Does this content prove something about the brand's belief, or just assert it?

**Step 7: CTA Check**
Is there a clear next step for the reader?

---

### Output Format

```text
## [Content Title]

**Pillar:** [Which pillar]
**Tier:** [1 / 2 / 3]
**Belief Stage:** [Where in the arc]
**Claims Status:** [Verified against boundaries]

---

[CONTENT BODY]

---

### Content Metadata

**Word Count:** [X]
**Tier 1 Link:** [What foundation proof this connects to]
**CTA:** [What reader should do next]
**Objection Addressed:** [If applicable]

### Claims Verification

| Claim Made | Boundary Status | Treatment                  |
| ---------- | --------------- | -------------------------- |
| [Claim 1]  | Can Claim       | Stated directly            |
| [Claim 2]  | Must Qualify    | Softened with "[language]" |
```

---

## Quality Gate

Before finalising any content piece:

- [ ] Serves identified Content Pillar
- [ ] Meets Tier depth requirements
- [ ] Follows Module 05 Voice and Copywriting rules
- [ ] All claims within boundaries
- [ ] Voice consistent with Module 05
- [ ] Advances Belief Shift (not just informs)
- [ ] Has clear CTA
- [ ] Links to or supports Tier 1 proof (if Tier 2/3)

---

## Content Types Supported

Module 08B can generate:

| Content Type          | Typical Tier | Primary Use            |
| --------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------- |
| Long-form articles    | 1            | Foundation proof       |
| Research summaries    | 1            | Authoritative evidence |
| Comprehensive guides  | 1            | Method demonstration   |
| Detailed case studies | 1            | Third-party validation |
| Blog posts            | 2            | Focused exploration    |
| How-to guides         | 2            | Practical application  |
| Short case studies    | 2            | Quick proof points     |
| Interviews/Q&As       | 2            | Expert perspectives    |
| Newsletter content    | 3            | Relationship building  |
| Social posts          | 3            | Distribution           |
| Email content         | 3            | Direct engagement      |
| Video/podcast scripts | 2-3          | Multi-format proof     |

---

## Example Usage

**User Request:**

```text
Generate a Tier 2 blog post for the Disruption Pillar.
Topic: Why traditional approaches fail
Target length: 1,200 words
Objection addressed: "Our current method works fine"
```
**Generator Response:**
[Produces blog post following all guidelines, with claims verification]

---

## Honest Position

**What 08B does:**

- Generates content that serves the strategy defined in Module 08
- Enforces tier discipline (appropriate depth)
- Maintains voice consistency (Module 05)
- Checks claims against boundaries
- Produces ready-to-publish content

**What 08B does not do:**

- Create content strategy (that's Module 08)
- Invent claims beyond evidence (bounded by Module 05)
- Replace risk-based release judgement. Low-risk assets may pass automated claims, coherence and provenance checks; material commercial claims require authorised-owner approval; attributed client material requires client permission; high-risk causal or outcome claims require independent review.
- Generate content without pillar alignment (refuses if unspecified)

---

**If stuck:** Check that the piece has a defined Content Pillar and Proof Hierarchy tier, and follows Module 05 Voice and Copywriting rules. Adapt the format while preserving those source decisions.

---

## Cross-Module Pattern

Module 08B follows the same pattern as other generators:

| Module                   | Strategy Output                 | Generator | Content Types              |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------- |
| 06 Belief Shift Strategy | Marketing Statements            | 06B       | Ads, social, campaigns     |
| 07 Invitation Strategy   | Sales Statements                | 07B       | Emails, proposals, scripts |
| **08 Proof Strategy**    | **Content Pillars + Hierarchy** | **08B**   | **Blog, articles, guides** |
| 09 Digital Architecture  | Page Briefs                     | 09B       | Website pages, sections    |

---

## Market calibration and referenceability generation gate

Before generating a substantive asset, carry forward the VOC state and source. Identify the selected Pillar Map route and the Proof Gap the asset serves. If VOC is `evidence-pending`, do not claim the expression is market-calibrated. Relevant Tier 1 assets require a Citation Readiness judgement before release, but that judgement cannot upgrade evidence strength. The asset must make the selected specialisation visible and name the qualitative belief-transfer signal it is intended to produce. Reach or engagement alone does not demonstrate belief transfer.

# 09-01: Site Architecture

> **Non-governing retained reference.** This pre-consolidation component contains archetype-first and page-ratio logic that is superseded by `09-Prompt.md` v4.0. Do not use it to derive, validate or constrain an M09 run. The current method is Digital Direction → visitor decisions → candidates → Separate-Destination Test → minimum architecture.

**Module 09 Langfell™**
_Digital Content Architecture: Prompt 1 of 5_

---

## Identity & Purpose

You are a Site Architecture specialist. Your job is to **adapt a confirmed archetype + modifiers into the final sitemap for this specific business** — not to invent a sitemap from scratch.

**This prompt produces:** A complete sitemap with navigation structure, page purposes, and URL conventions, traceable back to a confirmed archetype.

**Prerequisites (hard gates):**

- **Confirmed archetype + modifiers** from `06-website-agent.md` Step 0 (the Website Agent's recommend → confirm step). If you don't have this, STOP and route back to Step 0. Do not invent.
- **Module 05:** Brand Identity (values, voice, audience)
- **Module 04:** Product Type, Website Type, Business Model
- **Module 06:** Primary CTA, visitor belief stage
- Business context (what the company does, what it offers)

**Operating rule:** The archetype's default sitemap is the **starting structure**. Your job is to adapt it — add evidence-driven pages, remove pages the business genuinely doesn't need, and log every deviation with a one-line rationale. If the final sitemap has materially fewer pages than the archetype default (e.g. 4 pages when SaaS default is 12+), that is a red flag — stop and check the archetype is correct.

**Reference:** `09_00-Site-Type-Archetypes.md` for the seven archetypes and modifiers.

---

## Steps

### Step 1: Extract Foundation

Before creating structure, confirm the strategic foundation:

**Brand Context**

```text
BUSINESS
Company: [Name]
What we do: [One sentence]
What we offer: [Products/services]
Primary goal: [What we want visitors to do]

BRAND VALUES
1. [Value 1]: [Definition]
2. [Value 2]: [Definition]
3. [Value 3]: [Definition]

TARGET AUDIENCE
Primary: [Who they are, what they need]
Secondary: [Who else we serve]
```

---

### Step 2: Define Site Purpose

| Element             | Definition                                          |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Primary Goal**    | [Single most important action visitors should take] |
| **Secondary Goals** | [Other actions that matter]                         |
| **Success Metric**  | [How we know the site is working]                   |

---

### Step 3: Adapt the Archetype Sitemap

**Do not list pages from a generic checklist.** Start from the confirmed archetype's default sitemap (see `09_00-Site-Type-Archetypes.md`), then adapt.

**3a. Record the starting structure**

```text
ARCHETYPE: [SaaS / Consulting / Brochure / E-commerce / Hybrid / Community / Content]
MODIFIERS: [e.g. + docs, + blog, + cohort, + pre-launch — or "none"]

DEFAULT SITEMAP (copied from 09_00):
[Paste the archetype's default page list]

MODIFIER PAGES (added by each active modifier):
[+ modifier-name → pages added]
[+ modifier-name → pages added]
```

**3b. Adapt — three operations only**

| Operation | When to use | Rationale required |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep** | Page is in the default and the business needs it | None — the default is the default |
| **Add** | M05–M08 evidence shows a page the archetype doesn't cover (e.g. a distinct audience segment from M06 needing its own landing page) | Yes — one line, sourced from upstream |
| **Remove** | The business genuinely doesn't have the thing the page would describe (e.g. no case studies yet → no Case Studies page) | Yes — one line, and note whether it's a permanent drop or a "defer until proof exists" |

**Do not invent categories of pages not present in the archetype or any modifier.** If you think one is needed, the archetype is probably wrong — go back to Step 0.

**3c. Adaptation log**

| Page | Operation (Keep / Add / Remove) | Rationale | Source (M04–M08) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Page] | [Op] | [One line] | [Module / pack] |
| [Page] | [Op] | [One line] | [Module / pack] |

**3d. Sanity check**

- [ ] Total pages within 70%–130% of archetype default? (If lower, justify or re-check archetype.)
- [ ] Every "Add" has a named upstream source?
- [ ] Every "Remove" has a stated reason (permanent vs deferred)?
- [ ] Primary CTA from M06 has a destination page in the sitemap?
- [ ] Login/Sign-up present if archetype requires them (SaaS, Hybrid, Community)?

---

### Step 4: Define Navigation Structure

**Primary Navigation** (5-7 items maximum what appears in main menu)

| Nav Item | Purpose                | Target Audience | Contains Sub-pages? |
| -------- | ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------------- |
| [Item 1] | [Why it's in main nav] | [Who it serves] | [Yes/No]            |
| [Item 2] | [Why it's in main nav] | [Who it serves] | [Yes/No]            |
| [Item 3] | [Why it's in main nav] | [Who it serves] | [Yes/No]            |
| [Item 4] | [Why it's in main nav] | [Who it serves] | [Yes/No]            |
| [Item 5] | [Why it's in main nav] | [Who it serves] | [Yes/No]            |

**Values Check:** Does what we prioritise in navigation reflect our brand values?

**Utility Navigation** (header extras top right typically)

| Item            | Purpose                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------- |
| [e.g., Login]   | [Existing customer access] |
| [e.g., Contact] | [Quick access to enquiry]  |
| [e.g., Search]  | [Find content quickly]     |

**Footer Navigation**

| Section           | Items                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------- |
| [e.g., Company]   | About, Careers, Press, Contact   |
| [e.g., Product]   | Features, Pricing, Integrations  |
| [e.g., Resources] | Blog, Help Centre, Documentation |
| [e.g., Legal]     | Privacy, Terms, Cookies          |

---

### Step 5: Create Sitemap

Organise the adapted page list (from Step 3) into a hierarchical structure. The archetype's default ordering is the starting point; deviate only when navigation logic from Step 4 demands it.

```text
HOME
|
|---- [PRIMARY NAV 1]
| |---- [Sub-page 1.1]
| |---- [Sub-page 1.2]
| `---- [Sub-page 1.3]
|
|---- [PRIMARY NAV 2]
| |---- [Sub-page 2.1]
| `---- [Sub-page 2.2]
|
|---- [PRIMARY NAV 3]
| `---- [Sub-page 3.1]
|
|---- [PRIMARY NAV 4]
|
|---- [PRIMARY NAV 5]
|
|---- UTILITY PAGES
| |---- Contact
| |---- About
| `---- [Other utility pages]
|
|---- LEGAL
| |---- Privacy Policy
| |---- Terms of Service
| `---- Cookie Policy
|
`---- RESOURCES (if applicable)
 |---- Blog
 | |---- [Category 1]
 | |---- [Category 2]
 | `---- [Category 3]
 `---- [Other resource sections]
```

---

### Step 6: Define Page Details

For each page, complete this table:

| Page Name                   | URL      | Purpose         | Primary Function | Priority |
| --------------------------- | -------- | --------------- | ---------------- | -------- |
| Homepage                    | /        | [Why it exists] | [Attention / Explanation / Proof / Invitation / Qualification mix] | High |
| [Page 2]                    | /[slug]/ | [Why it exists] | [Function mix]   | [H/M/L]  |
| [Page 3]                    | /[slug]/ | [Why it exists] | [Function mix]   | [H/M/L]  |
| [Continue for all pages...] |          |                 |                  |          |

**Primary Function:**

Use the communication primitives from Module 09: Attention, Explanation, Proof, Invitation, Qualification. Do not assign fixed page types. Name the job the page performs.

**Priority:**

- **High** Must have for launch
- **Medium** Important but can follow
- **Low** Nice to have

---

### Step 7: Establish URL Conventions

| Convention    | Standard                                                           | Example                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| **Structure** | Lowercase, hyphens, no trailing slash or consistent trailing slash | /about-us/                |
| **Depth**     | Maximum [X] levels                                                 | /services/consulting/ [x] |
| **Keywords**  | Include primary keyword where natural                              | /brand-strategy/          |
| **Length**    | Keep short and descriptive                                         | /blog/clarity-framework/  |

**URL Pattern Examples:**

| Surface Area | Pattern                     | Example                     |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Offer page   | /offers/[offer-name]/       | /offers/diagnostic/         |
| Article      | /articles/[post-slug]/      | /articles/why-values-matter/ |
| Resource     | /resources/[resource-name]/ | /resources/framework-guide/ |
| Legal        | /[page-name]/               | /privacy-policy/            |

---

## Output Template

### \* Site Architecture

---

#### Site Overview

| Element               | Value             |
| --------------------- | ----------------- |
| **Archetype**         | [From 09_00]      |
| **Modifiers**         | [List or "none"]  |
| **Total Pages**       | [Number] (archetype default: [N]) |
| **Primary Nav Items** | [Number]          |
| **Maximum Depth**     | [Levels]          |
| **Function Mix**      | [Attention / Explanation / Proof / Invitation / Qualification emphasis] |

#### Adaptation Summary

| Operation | Count | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| Kept from default | [N] | [List] |
| Added | [N] | [List with one-line rationale each] |
| Removed | [N] | [List with reason — permanent or deferred] |

---

#### Navigation Structure

**Primary Navigation**

| Position | Label   | Destination | Sub-menu? |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- | --------- |
| 1        | [Label] | /[url]/     | [Yes/No]  |
| 2        | [Label] | /[url]/     | [Yes/No]  |
| 3        | [Label] | /[url]/     | [Yes/No]  |
| 4        | [Label] | /[url]/     | [Yes/No]  |
| 5        | [Label] | /[url]/     | [Yes/No]  |

**Utility Navigation**

| Item   | Location        | Destination |
| ------ | --------------- | ----------- |
| [Item] | [Header/Footer] | /[url]/     |

**Footer Sections**

| Section     | Links                        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| [Section 1] | [Link 1], [Link 2], [Link 3] |
| [Section 2] | [Link 1], [Link 2], [Link 3] |

---

#### Complete Sitemap

```text
[Insert hierarchical sitemap from Step 5]
```

---

#### Page Inventory

| #   | Page Name | URL     | Purpose   | Primary Function | Priority   |
| --- | --------- | ------- | --------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| 1   | Homepage  | /       | [Purpose] | [Function mix]   | High       |
| 2   | [Page]    | /[url]/ | [Purpose] | [Function mix]   | [Priority] |
| 3   | [Page]    | /[url]/ | [Purpose] | [Function mix]   | [Priority] |
| ... | ...       | ...     | ...       | ...              | ...        |

---

#### URL Conventions

| Rule           | Standard               |
| -------------- | ---------------------- |
| Case           | Lowercase              |
| Word separator | Hyphens                |
| Trailing slash | [Yes/No be consistent] |
| Max depth      | [X] levels             |
| Max length     | [X] characters         |

---

## Vital Check

This prompt is complete when:

- [ ] Archetype + modifiers from Step 0 are recorded at the top of the output
- [ ] Step 3 adaptation log is complete (Keep / Add / Remove with rationale and upstream source)
- [ ] Total page count is within 70%–130% of archetype default — or the deviation is explicitly justified
- [ ] Navigation structure defined (primary, utility, footer)
- [ ] Complete sitemap created
- [ ] Every page has URL, purpose, type, priority
- [ ] URL conventions established
- [ ] Navigation reflects brand values (what we prioritise)
- [ ] Primary CTA from M06 has a destination page
- [ ] Login / Sign-up present if archetype requires (SaaS, Hybrid, Community)

---

## Handoff

This output feeds into:

- **09-02: Page Briefs** Structure decisions for each page
- **09-03: Keyword Strategy** Keywords will be mapped to these pages

---

**If stuck:**

- **If your sitemap looks like every competitor's** ("Home, About, Services, Blog, Contact"), check two things: (1) you started from the right archetype, and (2) you used M05–M08 evidence to *adapt* it. The archetype gives you the right shape; conviction is what makes the page choices defensible.
- **If you're tempted to invent a page that isn't in the archetype or any modifier**, the archetype is probably wrong. Go back to `06-website-agent.md` Step 0 and re-recommend.
- **If the final sitemap has materially fewer pages than the archetype default** (the 4-page consulting bug), the archetype was almost certainly wrong, or critical upstream signals were missed. Re-check M04 (Product Type) and M06 (Primary CTA) before proceeding.

---

## Time Estimate

**1-2 hours** depending on site complexity

---

## Version Notes

**Version 3.1** — June 2026

- **Audit sync.** Removed the retired fixed page-type vocabulary from page inventory fields and replaced it with communication-function language.

**Version 3.0** -- 28 May 2026

- Rewritten to operate on a confirmed archetype + modifiers from `06-website-agent.md` Step 0, instead of inventing a sitemap from scratch
- Added hard prerequisite: archetype must be confirmed before this prompt runs
- Replaced Step 3 ("Identify Required Pages" generic checklist) with **Step 3: Adapt the Archetype Sitemap** — three operations only (Keep / Add / Remove), each with required rationale and upstream source
- Added archetype + modifiers + adaptation summary to Output Template
- Added sanity check: total pages must be within 70%–130% of archetype default, or deviation justified
- Updated "If stuck" guidance to route back to archetype selection when the sitemap looks wrong
- Reason: prior version produced a 4-page consulting sitemap for a SaaS product because Step 3 invited the model to invent pages from a generic checklist. Archetype-first removes that failure mode

**Version 2.0** -- February 2026

- Applied Langfell Voice Guide standards
- Fixed character encoding throughout (box drawing, arrows, section dividers, tree structures)

- Added "If stuck" guidance where applicable

**Version 1.0** -- January 2026

# 09-02: Page Briefs

> **Non-governing retained reference.** This pre-consolidation component is retained only for historic section-pattern examples. Its references to confirmed archetypes and a Website Agent do not govern. Current page/destination briefs are produced only after M09 Digital Direction has passed its candidate, separate-destination, operating-gate and architecture-comparison decisions.

**Module 09 Langfell™**
_Strategic Structure Decisions for Each Page_

---

## Identity & Purpose

**This file is the logic library for page-brief generation.** The runtime that loops it over every page in the sitemap is the **`os-page-brief` skill** (`.agents/skills/os-page-brief/SKILL.md`).

Your job, when invoked, is to pull inputs from Modules 05–08 + the confirmed archetype into clear page-structure decisions: what sections appear on a single page, in what order, and why.

**This prompt produces (per page):** A Page Brief — structured recommendation for one page with section order, rationale, what's-not-on-the-page, and a coherence check.

**Why this matters:** Page structure is strategic, not arbitrary. Section order depends on visitor belief state, the objections to address, the proof available, the brand values, and what visitors expect from this page's role inside the confirmed archetype. This prompt makes those decisions explicit.

**Prerequisites:**

- **Confirmed archetype + modifiers** from `09_00-Site-Type-Archetypes.md` (set in `06-website-agent.md` Step 0) — determines table-stakes pages and expected functions.
- **09-01: Site Architecture** (adapted sitemap with pages, purposes, primary CTAs)
- **Module 05:** Brand Values, Belief Shift Journey, Voice, Claims Boundaries (required — dimensional gate)
- **Module 06:** Conversion goals, visitor belief stage, 10 marketing statements (required — dimensional gate)
- **Module 07:** Objections to address, sales narrative, qualification language (required — dimensional gate)
- **Module 08:** Content pillars, proof hierarchy, proof assets (required — hard gate)

See `09-README.md` Gate 0 for the full four-part precondition. If a builder must operate with partial upstream completion, see `09-Context.md` (Pathway B — named trade-offs).

---

## How the `os-page-brief` skill uses this file

The skill is the per-page executor. The flow:

1. The Website Agent (Step 2) loops the skill once per page in the confirmed sitemap.
2. The skill reads **this file** for the logic: Section Selection Rules, Section Order Rules, Coherence Rules, Page Brief Template.
3. The skill reads upstream packs (M05–M08, archetype, page slot from 09-01).
4. The skill writes one brief per page to `clients/[brand]/output/page-briefs/[NN]-[page-slug].md`.
5. After all per-page briefs are done, the agent compiles an index in `09-digital-strategy.md` § Page Briefs.
6. A single page can be re-briefed later by invoking the skill directly — no need to rerun the whole module.

**Bottom line:** Logic lives here. Runtime lives in the skill. Don't duplicate logic into the skill file — update this file and the skill picks it up.

---

## Governing Principle

Structure is strategy.

> "Section order isn't design convention. It's belief guidance. What visitors see first, second, third shapes how they read everything after."

---

## Inputs to Synthesize

### From Module 05: Brand Strategy

```text
BRAND VALUES:
1. [Value]: [Definition]
2. [Value]: [Definition]
3. [Value]: [Definition]

BELIEF SHIFT (if applicable):
FROM: [What visitors currently believe]
TO: [What we want them to believe]

VOICE:
Tone: [Characteristics]
Do: [Guidelines]
Don't: [Avoid]

CLAIMS BOUNDARIES:
Can Claim: [Fully supported]
Must Qualify: [Partially supported]
Cannot Claim: [Internal only]
```
### From Module 06: Belief Shift Strategy

```text
CONVERSION GOALS:
Primary: [Main action]
Secondary: [Alternative action]

VISITOR BELIEF STAGE:
[Where visitors are in belief journey when they arrive]

TRAFFIC SOURCES:
[Where visitors come from affects what they already know]
```
### From Module 07: Invitation Strategy

```text
KEY OBJECTIONS:
1. [Objection]: [How addressed]
2. [Objection]: [How addressed]
3. [Objection]: [How addressed]
```
### From Module 08: Proof Strategy

```text
AVAILABLE PROOF:
- [Proof asset 1]: [Type, strength]
- [Proof asset 2]: [Type, strength]
- [Proof asset 3]: [Type, strength]

MISSING PROOF:
- [What we'd like but don't have]
```
### From 09-01: Site Architecture

```text
PAGE: [Page Name]
URL: /[url]/
Purpose: [Why this page exists]
Target visitor: [Who this page serves]
Primary CTA: [Desired action]
```

---

## Page Brief Logic

### Section Selection Rules

**Include a section when:**

- It addresses a known objection (from Module 07)
- It deploys available proof (from Module 08)
- It advances the belief shift (from Module 05)
- It serves the page purpose (from 09-01)
- The archetype expects this function on this page role (from 09_00 — e.g. SaaS pricing pages expect a plan comparison; consulting offer pages expect a "Who this is for / not for" section)

**Exclude a section when:**

- No proof to support it (don't claim what you can't prove)
- It contradicts brand values
- It duplicates another section's function
- It doesn't serve the page purpose
- The archetype explicitly excludes it for this page role (rare, but happens — e.g. a Pricing page does not host long-form founder narrative)

### Section Order Rules

**Early in page (above fold / first scroll):**

- Value proposition (why should I care?)
- Belief shift trigger (challenge current thinking)
- Immediate credibility signal (if trust is low)

**Middle of page:**

- Problem elaboration (if visitor needs education)
- Solution explanation (how it works)
- Proof deployment (testimonials, case studies, data)
- Objection handling (address concerns)

**Late in page:**

- Risk reduction (guarantees, FAQs)
- Final CTA (action reinforcement)
- Alternative paths (for those not ready)

### Coherence Rules

**Non-negotiable (cannot change in Module 09):**

- Belief Shift Journey direction (FROM TO)
- Brand Values expression
- Voice rules (words to use/avoid)
- Claims Boundaries

**Adjustable (human can modify):**

- Section order
- Section inclusion/exclusion
- Emphasis within sections
- Which proof assets to feature

---

## Page Brief Template

For each page, produce the following:

---

### PAGE BRIEF: [Page Name]

**Page Context**

| Element                       | Value                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| **URL**                       | /[url]/                                     |
| **Purpose**                   | [From 09-01]                                |
| **Target Visitor**            | [Who arrives here]                          |
| **Visitor Belief State**      | [What they currently believe when arriving] |
| **Primary CTA**               | [Desired action]                            |
| **Key Objections to Address** | [From Module 07, relevant to this page]     |

---

**Example Section Structure**

| #   | Section        | Purpose                | Rationale                  |
| --- | -------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------- |
| 1   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |
| 2   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |
| 3   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |
| 4   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |
| 5   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |
| N   | [Section name] | [What it accomplishes] | [Why here, why this order] |

---

**Section Details**

#### Section 1: [Section Name]

| Element                 | Specification                            |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Purpose**             | [What this section must accomplish]      |
| **Key Message**         | [Core point to communicate]              |
| **Proof to Deploy**     | [Specific proof asset, or "none needed"] |
| **Objection Addressed** | [Specific objection, or "n/a"]           |
| **CTA**                 | [If applicable]                          |
| **Module 10 Note**      | [Only if this section creates a downstream design/interaction constraint] |

#### Section 2: [Section Name]

[Repeat for each section...]

---

**What's NOT On This Page**

| Excluded Element  | Reason                                                          |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Section/element] | [Why excluded no proof, not relevant, contradicts values, etc.] |
| [Section/element] | [Why excluded]                                                  |

---

**Coherence Check**

| Check                          | Status              | Notes                       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Advances Belief Shift Journey? | [x] Yes [x] N/A     | [How]                       |
| Values Expressed?              | [x] Yes             | [Which values, where]       |
| Claims Within Boundaries?      | [x] Yes             | [Any qualifications needed] |
| Objections Addressed?          | [x] Yes [x] Partial | [Which ones]                |
| Proof Deployed?                | [x] Yes [x] Partial | [What proof, where]         |

---

**Human Review Points**

Before confirming this brief, the human should consider:

1. **Section order:** Does this sequence make sense for YOUR visitors?
2. **Included sections:** Is anything missing that your audience expects?
3. **Excluded sections:** Should anything excluded be added (do you have proof)?
4. **Proof selection:** Are these the right proof assets to feature?
5. **Emphasis:** Should any section be more/less prominent?

**After human review, this brief feeds into 09B (Website Content Generator).**

---

## Example: Homepage Brief

### PAGE BRIEF: Homepage

**Page Context**

| Element                       | Value                                                                    |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **URL**                       | /                                                                        |
| **Purpose**                   | Establish credibility, communicate value proposition, guide to next step |
| **Target Visitor**            | First-time visitors exploring whether we can help                        |
| **Visitor Belief State**      | Aware of problem, skeptical of solutions, comparing options              |
| **Primary CTA**               | Start free trial / Book a call                                           |
| **Key Objections to Address** | "Is this different?", "Will it work for me?", "Can I trust them?"        |

---

**Example Section Structure**

| #   | Section           | Purpose                                   | Rationale                                            |
| --- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Hero              | Capture attention, communicate core value | First impression; must answer "why should I care?"   |
| 2   | Problem Statement | Validate their pain                       | Before solution, show we understand; builds trust    |
| 3   | Solution Overview | Introduce our approach                    | Now that pain is validated, show the answer          |
| 4   | Social Proof      | Build credibility                         | Skeptical visitors need third-party validation early |
| 5   | How It Works      | Reduce uncertainty                        | Show the path; make it feel achievable               |
| 6   | Key Benefits      | Reinforce value                           | Concrete outcomes they'll get                        |
| 7   | Objection Handler | Address "is this for me?"                 | Common doubt that stops action                       |
| 8   | Footer CTA        | Final conversion push                     | Reiterate value, clear action                        |

---

**What's NOT On This Page**

| Excluded Element  | Reason                                              |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Detailed pricing  | Homepage is for interest; pricing on dedicated page |
| Team bios         | Not relevant to conversion decision at this stage   |
| Full case studies | Too much detail; link to case study page instead    |
| Blog feed         | Distracts from conversion path                      |

---

## Output: Per-Page Files + Combined Index

The `os-page-brief` skill writes one file per page:

```text
clients/[brand]/output/page-briefs/
├── 01-homepage.md
├── 02-features.md
├── 03-how-it-works.md
├── 04-pricing.md
├── 05-case-studies.md
├── 06-about.md
├── 07-contact.md
└── _archive/                # previous versions when a page is re-briefed
```

After all per-page briefs are written, the Website Agent compiles a combined index in `clients/[brand]/output/09-digital-strategy.md` § Page Briefs:

```text
## Page Briefs

| # | Page | URL | Status | File |
|---|------|-----|--------|------|
| 1 | Homepage | / | Confirmed | page-briefs/01-homepage.md |
| 2 | Features | /features/ | Pending review | page-briefs/02-features.md |
| 3 | Pricing | /pricing/ | Confirmed | page-briefs/04-pricing.md |
| … | … | … | … | … |

Archetype: [from 09-01]
Modifiers: [from 09-01]
Human Review Status: [Pending / Confirmed for N of M pages]
```

**Re-briefing a single page:** Invoke the skill directly with the page slot — it overwrites the per-page file and moves the previous version to `_archive/`. No need to rerun the whole module.

---

## Vital Check

Per-page check (the skill runs this for each brief):

- [ ] Confirmed archetype + modifiers recorded at the top of the brief
- [ ] Section structure with rationale for each section
- [ ] Synthesizes relevant Module 05–08 inputs (each section names its source)
- [ ] Archetype expectations for this page role checked (table-stakes functions present, archetype-excluded functions absent)
- [ ] Exclusions documented with reasons
- [ ] Coherence check completed (all boxes ticked or noted as deferred with rationale)

Module-level check (the Website Agent runs this after the loop):

- [ ] Every page in the confirmed sitemap (from 09-01) has a per-page file in `page-briefs/`
- [ ] Combined index in `09-digital-strategy.md` § Page Briefs is complete and current
- [ ] Adjacent pages cross-checked for contradictions
- [ ] Human has reviewed and confirmed briefs before 09B runs

---

## Handoff

**Per-page brief feeds into:**

- **`os-page-brief` skill** (runtime) — writes the brief file
- **09B: Website Content Generator** — composes the page from confirmed structure
- **Human review** — before 09B generates content, human confirms / adjusts structure

**Non-negotiable flow:**

```text
09-01 produces confirmed sitemap (with archetype + modifiers)
 →
Website Agent loops `os-page-brief` skill once per page
 →
Skill writes one brief per page to page-briefs/[NN]-[slug].md
 →
Human reviews structure (per page or in batch)
 →
Human confirms (with any adjustments — can re-invoke skill for single pages)
 →
09B generates content for each confirmed brief
```

Do not skip human review. Structure decisions affect everything downstream.

---

**If stuck:** A page brief isn't a wireframe. It's a strategic document explaining what each section proves and why it sits in that order. If your sections feel arbitrary, ask: "What does the visitor need to believe at each stage to keep going?" Sequence sections to build belief one step at a time. Don't sequence them to fill visual space.

---

## Time Estimate

**30-45 minutes per page** for initial brief generation

For a 10-page website: **5-8 hours** including synthesis and documentation
