# Quality Gates

## Strategy-to-action starter plans

Apply `FW_41`. A relevant accepted strategy's output set includes its recommended source-derived Starter Plan, exact opening and eleven sections, current hash/decision/consequence/evidence trace, separate recommendation class and human lifecycle, supported roles/dependencies/assets, conditional campaign requirements and specialist handoff. Reject generic tasks, invented budget/capacity/owners/calendar precision, missing qualifications or strategy changes hidden in planning. A required recommendation class does not mean the plan has been adopted. Record non-applicability rather than filling an irrelevant section. Existing gates and release permissions remain in force; local structural passes do not prove specialist usefulness or client comprehension.

> **Client-language translation gate:** Apply `FW_27` before passing any client-facing output. Preserve the visual decisions but translate framework labels into plain business language; fail if a capable client cannot state what has been decided, why, what it changes and what would make it return.

## Visual translation gate — required

Before M10 passes, a competent designer must be able to explain the intended experience after one reading of the Canonical Strategy, without further explanation from the strategist. The direction must also leave room for different designers to produce materially different solutions.

Pass only when the document contains creative idea, immediate plain-language translation, one-sentence designer brief, intended experience, Brand derivation, characteristic translations, visual behaviours, tensions/anti-territories, creative freedom and practitioner handoff. For each characteristic, require intended feeling, Brand-specific meaning, Think and Not this. Fail adjective lists that leave the reader to decode meaning, literal treatment of an analogy, prescribed imagery masquerading as an example, faux-SaaS delivery surfaces, anonymous-minimal restraint or a rough/documentary reading of `working material`.

## FW_32 accountability gate

For every material accepted decision, require an exact decision ID, complete Implementation Consequences, non-monetary Cost Drivers and a Decision Measurement Contract with intended effect, implementation proof, baseline requirement, evidence, attribution ceiling, evidence owner, review decisions, stop condition and narrowest return point. Fail a monetary estimate or `derivable` driver when concept, application set or production standard is unresolved; fail revenue/conversion causation or collapsed direction/production/publication/budget/spend states.

## Editorial Readability Gate

Apply `FW_27`. Pass only when practical visual meaning precedes the client's direction and device labels, every creative tension has a use/avoid application and Layer 1–7 remains outside the primary path. A designer must be able to identify fixed choices, freedom and stop conditions without decoding methodology. Record structural evidence; keep cold-client and cold-designer checks `pending`.

The final-refinement concept gate requires unlabelled recognition of the client's accepted direction, purposeful devices, the scoped priority applications, accessible non-colour state cues where relevant and the client's intended character. A named style, device, media set or consultancy character from a worked example cannot govern another client. Strategy text alone cannot pass these concept-dependent checks; keep them `pending` until designed work exists.

## Runtime Derivation Boundary Gate

Pass only when the response uses exact accepted Module 05 anchors and the current RouteAuthorization, derives only the requested layer or artefact, and distinguishes fixed, flexible and unresolved decisions. Fail silent completion of later layers, a final style system, production specification or image prompts.

Aspirational or unapproved identity remains explicitly exploratory and cannot lock direction or brief production. Fail any visual choice presented as proof of quality, any unsupported proof claim, or category convention substituted for accepted identity. A compliant refusal returns to evidence-derived visual direction.

Stop and return language must state the boundary, reason and next decision plainly. Exposed internal gate names or a newly introduced method label fail the client-facing response.

## Strategy Multi-View Gate

For each routed Visual view, apply `FW_26`: verify standard metadata and state inheritance; preserve the creative recommendation, inherited obligations, visual ranges, operating modes, proof honesty, trade-off and accepted decision; require the Executive View to support leadership understanding without a second approval request; require a 7–10-slide narrative with speaker notes and source trace. Reject any implication that creative direction is final visual production.

Verify the visual direction reflects every fixed business-definition field in the approved Business Foundation, remains compatible with its Business Manifesto and expresses the canonical Module 05 strategy without redefining the business. It must give the worldview form rather than literalise declarations or create a competing belief system. A missing, stale or mismatched Business Foundation blocks the module and returns to the owning source.

## Module 10: Visual Identity

## Consultancy Judgement Gate

Pass only when the first page states the visual-investment recommendation; evidence and confidence are explicit; credible design routes have been compared; the accepted trade-off, client decision, conditions, owner, progression and invalidation are clear; and the complete Consultancy Decision Record has been checked transiently with its final state recorded compactly in `RUN-MANIFEST.md`. A moodboard menu, premature asset programme or blurred direction/production state fails `CMQG_05`.

Quality Gates check that outputs derive from conviction before they pass to the next module. They catch generic work before other modules build on it.

These gates track the **seven-layer derivation chain** (see `10-Visual-Style-Framework.md`). Each gate verifies one layer's output and confirms it traces to a verbatim upstream anchor. There is no "style selection" gate — selecting a visual position from the 12 named styles instead of deriving it is an automatic fail.

---

## How to Use Quality Gates

1. **Complete the layer** -- Run the relevant part of `10-Prompt.md`, generate the layer output
2. **Run the Quality Gate** -- Check all items for that gate
3. **If all pass** -- Proceed to the next layer
4. **If any fail** -- Revise before proceeding

**Complete every gate.** Check each layer’s derivation before downstream work makes corrections more costly.

## Client Output Gate

Before lock, verify the exact practical Visual Strategy headings in `FW_26`, the transient seven-layer derivation check and complete evaluation contract exist. Record only the compact pass/fail result and source hash in `RUN-MANIFEST.md`. A client must pass the ninety-second comprehension test without decoding layer names. Do not render approved derivatives before the canonical strategy is accepted and locked. After acceptance, `10-visual-strategy-practitioner-brief.md` must use Practitioner Brief V3 (`view-version: 3.0.0`, `format: Langfell-hybrid-practitioner-brief`) and apply `10-Visual-Practitioner-Brief-Prompt.md`: it must preserve the common spine and let a cold competent designer teach back the assignment, governing rule, six project-specific Visual Contract commitments, fixed/flexible/unresolved decisions, creative latitude, scope-appropriate routes, derived applications, evaluation, stop and change-control rules in five minutes. It must pass project-specificity, Visual Contract integration, no-new-strategy and shared-lock checks. `creative-direction-locked` must not be presented as `visual-system-locked`, production approval or publication approval. Internal control material in the primary client body or a default standalone internal file fails the gate.

### Visual Exploration Pack gate

After Visual Strategy lock, `<brand-or-project>-visual-exploration-pack.md` must apply `10-Visual-Exploration-Pack-Prompt.md`. Pass only when it inherits the exact primary source, version, lock and approval event; uses this client's six Visual Contract positions; derives categories and applications from current scope; supplies a reusable global prefix, two to four prompts per selected category, organising-device exploration where applicable, anti-reference prompts, a proportionate generation plan, keep/reject curation criteria, stylescape assembly and concept handoff; and clearly excludes final design and automatic image generation. Run source-fidelity, Visual Contract, client-specificity, exploration-not-execution, application-relevance, anti-reference, designer-usefulness, copyright-safety and stale-view checks. Generic “modern, clean, premium” prompts, named-artist imitation, copyrighted branded material, another client's vocabulary or any final-logo/final-identity request fails the gate.

**Response Path note:** under a Module 04 `RouteAuthorization` `Accept the Constraint` (lighter version) path, Gates 2–3 (Layers 4–5 numeric narrowing) are marked **N/A** — the module runs Layers 2–3 at principle level only, declares Expressive by default, and does not scale up 10B. Gates 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 still apply.

---

## Cross-Module Canonical Gates Applied Here

The following canonical Quality Gates from `framework/FW_17-Cross-Module-Quality-Gates.md` apply to this module:

- **CMQG_01 Conviction Trace** — **yes.** Every layer output must trace back to Module 05's Brand Strategy (which carries Module 01 lineage via Module 03). Trace through the locked Module 05 Handoff Pack; do not read Module 01 directly.
- **CMQG_02 Claims Boundary Compliance** — **yes.** Every visual element that makes a public claim (proof imagery, certification marks, before/after compositions, results-display chrome, comparison visuals, photography subject choices) must fall within Module 01 / Module 05 Claims Boundaries. Visual overclaim is permanent.
- **CMQG_03 Upstream Acknowledgment Satisfaction** — **— (not applicable).** Per FW_17 per-module table, no R-pattern Acknowledgments from Module 02 Gate 5 are routed to Module 10. Any Acknowledgments inherited via the upstream chain pass through unchanged.
- **CMQG_04 Translation Trace** — **yes.** Every layer output (Layers 2–7 + Exploration Layer + Layer 7 artefact) must pair with a verbatim upstream anchor per the Per-Layer Source-Anchor Mapping table in `10-Prompt.md` Translation Discipline section. The seven-layer derivation chain is itself a structured implementation of CMQG_04.

Module-specific Quality Gates (below) cover tests unique to Module 10.

---

## Gate 0: Governance Check (Before Starting)

This gate has three parts. **Part A** (Completeness) checks that Module 05 has produced all required outputs. **Part B** (Anchoring) checks that those outputs are genuinely anchored rather than aspirational. **Part C** (RouteAuthorization) checks that the approved route and `generation_permission` permit the visual work. See `10-README.md` Gate 0 for the anchoring check in detail.

### Part A: Completeness (Is Module 05 Done?)

| Check | Pass | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module 05 Brand Strategy complete (carries translated Core Belief + Positioning) | Strategy statement written | Missing or generic |
| Module 05 Brand Personality complete | 3-5 traits defined | Missing or generic |
| Module 05 Values complete | 3-5 values with meanings | Missing or generic |
| Module 05 Voice complete | Voice characteristics defined | Missing |
| Module 05 Filter complete | For/Not For defined | Missing |

### Part C: RouteAuthorization (Is the route approved and scope clear?)

| Check | Pass | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module 04 RouteAuthorization present | `route`, `status`, `capability_profile`, `authorised_human_decision`, `decision_owner`, `closure_conditions`, `permitted_*`, `generation_permission` documented | Missing |
| `status` is `Approved` or `Overridden` | Visual system can lock | Route not approved — draft only |
| `generation_permission` matches intent | `publish-ready` for public 10B outputs; `draft-only` for non-public | Publish attempted without permission |

### Part B: Anchoring (Is Module 05 Anchored or Aspirational?)

| Check | Pass | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brand Personality describes actual behaviour | Traits evidenced in operations/delivery | Traits the business wishes it had |
| Values describe actual operations | Values evidenced in how business behaves | Values the business aspires to |
| Voice reflects actual writing today | How the business actually sounds | How the business wishes it sounded |
| Filter reflects real trade-offs | Business has actually disqualified "Not For" group | Filter written but never applied |
| Brand Strategy references demonstrations | Specific operations/results cited | Manifesto without proof |

### Reading the Anchoring Verdict (Ternary, not Binary)

The five rows in Part B each produce a per-row signal: **Anchored** or **Aspirational**. Aggregate them:

| Pattern | Verdict | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All 5 rows Anchored | **Anchored** | Proceed. The visual identity derived will express real character — and to the extent the underlying conviction is itself distinctive, competitors can't copy it without adopting that conviction. Gate 0 confirms anchoring, not distinctiveness: a brand can be honestly anchored to generic convictions, and the chain will translate generic-in to generic-out. Distinctiveness comes from Module 01, not from Module 10. |
| 1–2 rows Aspirational, rest Anchored | **Partial** | Proceed **only** by deriving visual identity from the anchored rows. Aspirational territory is omitted from visual expression entirely — not flagged-and-shipped. The resulting visual identity will be quieter than ambition wants; that is the correct outcome. If that is not acceptable, treat as Aspirational. |
| 3+ rows Aspirational | **Aspirational** | **Stop.** Return to Modules 01–04, complete the gates properly, re-lock Module 05. |

**If Part A fails (Completeness):** Cannot proceed. Return to Module 05 and complete the missing outputs.

**If Part B verdict is Aspirational:** Cannot proceed. Do not build visual identity on aspirational brand identity — it is the most publicly damaging form of overclaim the framework can produce. Visual identity ships as a single unitary expression; there is no seam between the anchored and aspirational parts when the audience sees it.

**If Part B verdict is Partial:** Proceed under the strict scoping rule above. Visual identity must not overclaim what the business hasn't yet demonstrated. See `10-README.md` Gate 0 for the matching verdict structure.

---

## \* Gate 1: Layers 2–3 (Spatial Logic + Resonance Position)

### Layer 2 — Spatial Logic

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focal logic stated as principle | Not jumped to specifics | [ ] |
| Containment stated as principle | How the brand holds/frames | [ ] |
| Breathing stated as principle | How the brand uses space/rhythm | [ ] |
| Each property opens with a verbatim Module 05 anchor | Quote precedes the derived statement | [ ] |
| Each statement names the quoted word(s) it derives from | Visible trace, not "captured in spirit" | [ ] |

### Layer 3 — Resonance Position (six binary pairs)

| Axis | Binary commitment made? | Names the quoted word(s) that compelled it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm / Cool | [ ] | [ ] |
| Spacious / Dense | [ ] | [ ] |
| Calm / Energetic | [ ] | [ ] |
| Restrained / Expressive | [ ] | [ ] |
| Clean / Raw | [ ] | [ ] |
| Focused / Layered | [ ] | [ ] |

**No-spectrum guardrail:**

> "Did any axis come out as 'kind of warm' or 'somewhat spacious'?"

- [ ] No spectrum language — every axis is a clean binary commitment

**If spectrum language appears:** Module 05 is under-specified, or the Step 1 quotation is missing the discriminating phrase. Return to Module 05 — do not split the difference with the named-style menu.

---

## \* Gate 2: Layer 4 (Design Behaviour Translation)

*N/A under Module 04 Accept-the-Constraint (lighter version).*

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every commitment translated | Intent, behaviours, verification, failure signals and retained freedom | [ ] |
| Behaviours trace to a Layer 3 position and Module 05 anchor | Translation follows strategy, not preference | [ ] |
| Structure precedes styling | Hierarchy, sequence and relationships do not rely on colour, imagery or motion to work | [ ] |
| No premature specification | No typeface, colour, grid, spacing value or finished asset is selected without production authority | [ ] |

---

## \* Gate 3: Layer 5 (Context Narrowing)

*N/A under Module 04 Accept-the-Constraint (lighter version).*

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sub-Input 5a (Sector) applied | Own reasoning recorded | [ ] |
| Sub-Input 5b (Medium) applied | Own reasoning recorded | [ ] |
| Sub-Input 5c (Audience reading pattern) applied | Own reasoning recorded | [ ] |
| External Constraints noted | Accessibility / regulatory / platform — or "none applicable" | [ ] |
| Contextual guidance recorded for material behaviours | Per-sub-input reasoning preserved, not collapsed into one justification | [ ] |

---

## \* Gate 4: Layer 6 (Operating Model Declared)

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operating Model declared | Expressive **or** Controlled — explicit, not implicit | [ ] |
| Decision criteria stated | Sector trust, audience trust sensitivity, conviction posture, distribution | [ ] |
| Rationale recorded | Why this declaration follows from the criteria | [ ] |
| Secondary Mode Zones scoped (if hybrid) | Named surfaces only, bounded by the Visual Signature Label | [ ] |

**The fork test:**

> "Does Layer 7's output structure follow from this declaration (Style System if Controlled, Operating Constitution if Expressive)?"

- [ ] Yes — the declaration is load-bearing, not decorative

---

## \* Gate 5: Exploration Layer (Three Variation Strategies)

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three variation strategies authored | Not one direction with colour swaps | [ ] |
| Locked axes vs free axes named | Each strategy explores only the free axes | [ ] |
| Each strategy stays coherent with locked axes | No strategy invents a new axis position | [ ] |
| Each strategy is meaningfully distinct | Three genuine routes through the free axes | [ ] |

**Human Confirmation Required (non-negotiable):**

- [ ] Builder has reviewed the three strategies and **selected one** before proceeding
- [ ] The two rejected strategies are documented

**If not confirmed:** Do not proceed to Layer 7 or 10B.

---

## \* Gate 6: Layer 7 Artefact

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correct artefact for the Operating Model | Style System if Controlled, Operating Constitution if Expressive | [ ] |
| Visual Signature Label present | 2–4 owned words, not one of the 12 named styles or a synonym | [ ] |
| Signature Label is traceable | Lists the Layer 3 positions + Layer 1 inputs that produced it | [ ] |
| All required components included | Per the framework's Layer 7 component list | [ ] |
| Derivation Chain Record complete | Every Layer 7 decision traceable to a Layer 1 input through the intermediate layers | [ ] |
| Claims Boundaries cross-check passed | Every public-claim visual verified against Module 01 / 05 Claims Boundaries | [ ] |

### Derivation Verification (layer trace)

| Layer 7 element | Traces back through | Verified? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spatial Logic | Module 05 Personality / Values / Filter / Voice (Layer 2) | [ ]/[ ] |
| Resonance Position | Module 05 Personality / Values / Voice / Filter (Layer 3) | [ ]/[ ] |
| Behaviour and contextual guidance | Layer 3 → Layer 4 → Layer 5 | [ ]/[ ] |
| Operating Model | Module 03 positioning + Module 05 Brand Strategy / Personality / Audience + Module 04 Response Path (Layer 6) | [ ]/[ ] |
| Boundary statements ("never does") | Module 03 COMMIT row via Module 05 + Filter (Not For) | [ ]/[ ] |
| Visual Signature Label | Layer 1 conviction + Layer 3 positions | [ ]/[ ] |

---

## \* Gate 7: Two-Part Coherence Test

Before completing Module 10, run both parts of the Ultimate Test. Each checks a different failure and has its own repair path.

**Part 1 — Expression:** "If someone saw only the visual identity (no words), would they sense _any_ specific conviction at all?"

- [ ] Yes — visual expresses _a_ conviction
- [ ] No — visual reads as decoration, generic, or empty

**Part 2 — Correctness:** "If yes to Part 1, is the conviction they would sense _this brand's_ conviction (the Module 05 anchor) — not a different one?"

- [ ] Yes — visual expresses _this_ conviction
- [ ] No — visual expresses _a_ conviction but it's the wrong one

| Result | Diagnosis | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Part 1 No | Visual is decoration, not derivation | Re-derive from Module 05 inputs — add expression where it's missing |
| Part 1 Yes, Part 2 No | Visual expresses a conviction, but the wrong one | Identify which conviction the visuals currently express, then replace expression — adding more won't fix this; only replacement will |
| Both Yes | Visual proves conviction | Pass |

**Why split:** the binary form ("yes/no, does this work?") conflated two different failures with different repair paths. Adding more visual signal cannot fix the wrong-signal case, and replacing signal is the wrong move when no signal exists at all. A reader who answers "kind of" to the old binary test is almost always in the wrong-conviction case, not the no-conviction case.

**Test only the dimensions in use.** Some brands use no motion or no imagery beyond a logo. Exclude absent dimensions from the test, as defined in `10-Philosophy.md` v3.4 *Visual Identity Is Five Distinct Dimensions*.

### Layer 7 Output Artefact Check

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Style System or Operating Constitution declared | Locked or principled output present | [ ] |
| Principles / Tokens / Implementation separated | Three distinct sections in the artefact | [ ] |
| Tokens are named and platform-agnostic | `colour-primary`, `type-scale-1`, `space-4`, etc. | [ ] |
| Implementation examples reference tokens, not redefine them | Web / print / motion / packaging examples use token names | [ ] |
| Accessibility notes included | Contrast, readable sizes, focus states, reduced-motion preference | [ ] |
| RouteAuthorization field copied from M04 | `route`, `status`, `capability_profile`, `generation_permission` recorded | [ ] |

### Accessibility Check

- [ ] Minimum contrast ratio for text/UI components meets WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text/UI)
- [ ] Type scale includes a readable body size and accessible heading hierarchy
- [ ] Focus states and reduced-motion preference are addressed for digital implementation
- [ ] No visual claim (proof imagery, certification marks, etc.) oversteps Module 05 Claims Boundaries

If any accessibility check fails, the Layer 7 artefact cannot lock for public implementation.

---

## \* Gate 8: Ready for 10B + Visual Contract Outputs

| Criterion | Evidence | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layer 7 artefact locked | Critique Loop passed; artefact is canonical source | [ ] |
| All 10B generations will derive from the Layer 7 artefact | Never from upstream layers directly | [ ] |
| Visual Contract Brief generated | From the six locked Layer 3 positions | [ ] |
| Evaluation Companion generated | From the six locked Layer 3 positions | [ ] |
| Ready for Pilot Phase / Module 11 | Handoff Pack complete (see `10-Handoff-Pack.md`) | [ ] |

---

## Fail Conditions

### Automatic Fail

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A layer was skipped (output is a disguised selection) | FAIL -- return to the skipped layer and re-derive downward |
| Visual position selected from the 12 named-style menu, not derived | FAIL -- derive through the layers; named styles are reference vocabulary only |
| Spectrum language smuggled into Layer 3 ("kind of warm") | FAIL -- return to Module 05; commit to a binary |
| A layer output can't be traced to a verbatim upstream anchor | FAIL -- push the source quotation back in (CMQG_04) |
| Operating Model left implicit | FAIL -- declare Expressive or Controlled explicitly |
| Derivation Chain Record incomplete | FAIL -- every Layer 7 decision must trace to a Layer 1 input |
| Builder hasn't selected a variation strategy | FAIL -- get sign-off before Layer 7 / 10B |
| Visual element overclaims beyond Claims Boundaries | FAIL -- visual overclaim is permanent; cut it |
| Two-Part Coherence Test: Part 1 No or Part 2 No | FAIL -- see the diagnosis-and-fix table |

### Recovery

| Failure | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Layer skipped | Return to that layer, complete it, re-derive downward |
| Selected from style menu | Re-run `10-Prompt.md` with full inputs; derive through the layers |
| Spectrum language | Return to Module 05 — find the discriminating phrase |
| Missing trace | Quote the upstream anchor verbatim, then re-derive the layer output |
| Operating Model implicit | Run the Layer 6 decision matrix and declare |
| Part 1 No | Add expression where missing — re-derive from Module 05 |
| Part 1 Yes, Part 2 No | Replace expression — identify the wrong conviction, swap it for this brand's |

---

## Failure-Mode Catalogue

These examples show the failures the existing gates are designed to catch.

### 1. Gate 0: The Aspirational Identity Ships

**What happened:** a founder says the brand is "clinical, evidence-led, and precise," but the business still sells mostly through warm founder trust and undocumented delivery.

**What breaks:** the designer builds a visual identity that looks like a regulated medical product. Prospects expect clinical proof the business cannot provide.

**How it is caught:** Gate 0 marks Brand Personality and Values as Aspirational. Module 10 stops before visual work starts.

**Recovery cost:** high if already shipped. Re-lock Module 05, remove unsupported proof signals, and replace public assets that created the overclaim.

### 2. Gate 1: Spectrum Language Gets Through

**What happened:** the Resonance Position reads "somewhat warm, fairly clean, a little expressive."

**What breaks:** one designer makes it friendly, another makes it restrained, and both can defend their choice because the source never committed.

**How it is caught:** Gate 1 fails the no-spectrum guardrail.

**Recovery cost:** moderate before Layer 7, high after design production. Return to Module 05 and find the phrase that forces the binary.

### 3. Gate 3: Context Narrowing Was Skipped

**What happened:** the website spacing works on desktop, then the same spacious system is applied to mobile reports and sales decks.

**What breaks:** the brand still looks "on strategy" but becomes hard to use where the audience scans under pressure.

**How it is caught:** Gate 3 shows Sector, Medium, and Audience reasoning collapsed into one generic rationale.

**Recovery cost:** low to medium. Re-run Layer 5 for the affected media and regenerate the relevant 10B outputs.

### 4. Gate 4: Operating Model Was Left Implicit

**What happened:** the website is tightly controlled, social posts are expressive, slide decks drift between the two, and nobody knows which one is correct.

**What breaks:** the brand starts to look inconsistent even though individual pieces are well designed.

**How it is caught:** Gate 4 has no explicit Expressive or Controlled declaration, or no scoped Secondary Mode Zones.

**Recovery cost:** medium. Declare the Primary Operating Model, name any Secondary Mode Zones, and re-issue the Layer 7 artefact.

### 5. Gate 7: The Visuals Express the Wrong Conviction

**What happened:** the identity is distinctive and memorable, but it signals rebellion when the brand's actual conviction is careful repair.

**What breaks:** adding more polish makes the problem worse, because the wrong signal is being strengthened.

**How it is caught:** Gate 7 Part 1 passes but Part 2 fails.

**Recovery cost:** high. Replace the expression. Do not add more visual devices to it.

### 6. Claims Boundary: Visual Proof Overclaims

**What happened:** a proof-heavy visual system uses before/after imagery, result badges, or certification-style marks the business cannot support.

**What breaks:** the visual identity creates a public claim the copy would never be allowed to make.

**How it is caught:** CMQG_02 and Gate 6 Claims Boundaries cross-check fail.

**Recovery cost:** variable. Remove the unsupported proof signal immediately; if the asset has shipped widely, log the correction in Module 11/12 tracking.

---

## Summary: All Gates

| Gate  | Layer / Stage | Key Question |
| ----- | ------------- | ------------ |
| 0     | Before starting | Is Module 05 complete and Anchored (or Partial)? |
| 1     | Layers 2–3 | Spatial Logic + six Resonance commitments, each traced to a verbatim anchor? |
| 2     | Layer 4 | Design behaviours, verification and retained freedom derived from the Layer 3 positions? |
| 3     | Layer 5 | Sector × medium × audience adaptations recorded per material behaviour? |
| 4     | Layer 6 | Operating Model declared Expressive or Controlled? |
| 5     | Exploration | Three distinct coherent strategies; builder selected one? |
| 6     | Layer 7 | Correct artefact + Visual Signature Label + complete Derivation Chain Record? |
| 7     | Coherence | Two-Part Test: visual expresses _this_ brand's conviction? |
| 8     | Ready for 10B | Layer 7 locked; Visual Contract outputs generated; handoff ready? |

---

## Quality Criteria — Not All Equal Weight

Three gates are non-negotiable. Failing any one fails the module, regardless of how many other criteria pass.

| Gate | Non-Negotiable? |
| --- | --- |
| Gate 0: Governance | **Yes** — an Aspirational verdict stops the module |
| Gate 1: Layers 2–3 | No (diagnostic) |
| Gate 2: Layer 4 | No (diagnostic; N/A under lighter path) |
| Gate 3: Layer 5 | No (diagnostic; N/A under lighter path) |
| Gate 4: Layer 6 | No (diagnostic) |
| Gate 5: Exploration | **Yes** — builder selection of a variation strategy is required before Layer 7 / 10B |
| Gate 6: Layer 7 | No (diagnostic) — but Derivation Chain Record completeness is checked here |
| Gate 7: Two-Part Coherence | **Yes** — both parts must pass; Part 1 No or Part 2 No fails the module |
| Gate 8: Ready for 10B | No (diagnostic) |

The diagnostic gates help locate the source of a failure. Passing them cannot compensate for failure at any of the three non-negotiable gates.

---

## Founder, catalyst and execution gate

Pass only when applicable founder cues derive from Module 05 or carry a reasoned `not-applicable` state; every used Visual Catalyst has been traced and rederived rather than copied; the custom style is documented well enough to execute consistently; and material visual decisions pass the visual referenceability test. Fail moodboard authority, aesthetic mimicry, generic founder imagery or literal citation marks imposed on visual outputs.

## Version Notes

**Version 3.9** — 17 August 2026

- Added the Practitioner Brief V3 format and common-spine checks without weakening the Visual Contract actionability gate.

**Version 3.8** — 27 July 2026

- Added a plain-language stop/return check to prevent internal gate-name leakage.

- Added explicit exploratory-state and visual-proof boundaries.

**Version 3.1** — 19 June 2026

- **Added Failure-Mode Catalogue.** The gates now include six concrete failure stories keyed to Gate 0, Gate 1, Gate 3, Gate 4, Gate 7, and Claims Boundary failure, with recovery costs named.

**Version 3.0** — 29 May 2026

- **Restructured the gates around the seven-layer derivation chain.** v2.x kept the old per-output gate set (Visual Strategy → Colour Philosophy → Typography Philosophy → Imagery Direction → Design Principles → **Style Recommendation** → Design Philosophy → Handoff Pack) even after the framework, prompt, and Handoff Pack moved to the seven layers. The gates now track Layers 2–7 + Exploration + Ready-for-10B, matching `10-Handoff-Pack.md` v4.x gate numbering exactly.
- **Removed the "Style Recommendation / Style Selection" gate.** Selecting a position from the 12 named styles instead of deriving it is now an automatic fail, not a gate.
- **Added Visual Contract outputs** (Brief + Evaluation Companion) to Gate 8.
- **Preserved** Gate 0 (ternary anchoring verdict), the CMQG mapping, the two-part Ultimate Test (now Gate 7), the surface-conditional caveat, and the non-negotiable-weighting principle.

# Module 10 Strategy Schema

## Strategy-to-action starter plans

Apply `FW_41`. Keep the existing strategy fields and schema version; attach the separately versioned `strategy-to-action: 1.0` transport defined in `templates/strategy-to-action/plan.schema.json` through `starter-plan-refs` in the handoff/private manifest. A plan references the existing decision, consequence and evidence records. Those records retain authority over strategy fields. The corresponding recommended Starter Plan is a derived output after source acceptance. Human adoption, production and release remain separate. No legacy locked strategy is silently rewritten or automatically reapproved.

## FW_32 source-owned accountability records

The internal canonical state adds `material_decisions`, `assumptions`, `implementation_consequences`, `cost_drivers` and `decision_measurement_contracts` using the exact schemas in `framework/FW_32-Strategy-Accountability-Implementation-and-Decision-Support-Contract.md`. Client views may explain selected effects and implementation implications but do not expose raw governance schemas.

For every material concept, system, application and production decision, record the intended effect, consequence and rule for the next decision. Cost Drivers contain units, complexity, delivery model and production standard but no rates. Unresolved concept, application set or standard forces `not-yet-estimable`.

## Editorial read-contract — required

Canonical outputs add every editorial field in `FW_27`. Explain the practical visual meaning before naming `Restrained Clarity`, and the visible relationship before naming `Source Trace`. The application contract requires unlabelled recognisability, meaningful rather than compulsory Source Trace, website/document/publishing proof, non-colour evidence-state cues and a human-led consultancy character distinct from a creator brand. Creative tensions carry use/avoid guidance. Seven-layer method trace is checked transiently and is not a default document output.

Structural checks may pass the language, framework-purpose, redundancy, terminology and qualification fields. Cold-reader and designer comprehension remain `pending` until tested.

## Governed strategy outputs

The client-readable **Visual Strategy** and canonical authority is `10-visual-strategy.md`. Before client decision, explain that acceptance will generate the four standard views—Executive View (`10-visual-strategy-executive-view.md`), Strategic Snapshot (`10-visual-strategy-strategic-snapshot.md`), Presentation View (`10-visual-strategy-presentation-view.md`) and Practitioner Brief (`10-visual-strategy-practitioner-brief.md`)—plus the **Visual Exploration Pack**, `<brand-or-project>-visual-exploration-pack.md`. Do not emit them as approved derivatives until the Canonical Strategy is accepted and locked. Every output inherits the same canonical states, source, version, lock ID and approval event. Generate each from the primary file and transient view-source state. Generate the Practitioner Brief through `10-Visual-Practitioner-Brief-Prompt.md` using schema `1.2`, `view-version: 3.0.0`, `format: Langfell-hybrid-practitioner-brief`, the common V3 spine and the complete Visual-specific middle. Generate the Visual Exploration Pack through `10-Visual-Exploration-Pack-Prompt.md`. The pack has schema `visual-exploration-pack` version `1.0`, `view-type: creative-exploration`, `production-state: approved-for-exploration` and is not one of the four standard strategy views. It may generate images only after an explicit user request. The Canonical Strategy replaces the former Comprehensive View.

**This contract defines the locked structure that downstream skills read.** `10-Handoff-Pack.md` specifies which outputs pass downstream and why. This schema specifies where skills can find each output in the M10 visual-identity document.

The client document uses practical headings. The seven-layer derivation chain is assembled and checked in transient runtime state. Downstream skills read the canonical fields and reconstruct the internal mapping only when required.

**Schema version: 1.3.** Pin this in `dmode.config.md` (`m10-strategy: 1.3`). Skills declare the schema version they were built against; a mismatch is a compatibility check, not a silent failure.

> **M10 is principle-level direction, not design execution.** M10 produces a defensible *visual logic* (axes, spatial rules, operating model) traceable to M05 verbatim — not fonts, palettes or logos. Design execution is the designer's job; 10B generates the *briefs* that hand that logic to them. Keep that line (see arch §6.1, "Level 2 not Level 3").

> **Audience note.** `10-visual-strategy.md` is the complete client working strategy. Its primary headings follow the Visual Strategy client contract in `FW_26`; internal layer mapping is not emitted by default. The role-specific Visual Designer Brief is the direct execution surface.

---

## Client output wrapper — required

Begin with the creative idea, immediately translate it into plain language, then give a one-sentence designer brief and intended experience before explaining derivation. Every characteristic uses `Characteristic`, `Intended feeling`, `Brand-specific meaning`, `Think` and `Not this`. Describe visual behaviours through what the identity must make visible or understandable, leaving the choice of device open. Follow with tensions/anti-territories, creative freedom and practitioner handoff. The primary client body must not contain internal controls, moodboards, references, concept routes or technical specification; keep layer names and machine controls transient and record only compact source/state results in the manifest. `creative-direction-locked` and `visual-system-locked` remain separate production states.

Required client-file metadata fields: `document-state`, `client-decision-state`, `evidence-state`, `source-authority-state`, `production-state`. Legacy status fields are prohibited in client-rendered files. Keep richer lifecycle states transient and persist only their compact result in the run manifest. A recommended creative direction must not be described as accepted or locked in the client body.

## Consultancy Decision Record — internal handoff only

Canonical fields: `decision_id`, `module`, `decision_area`, `situation`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_status`, `confidence`, `diagnosis`, `options_considered`, `comparison_criteria`, `recommendation`, `rationale`, `accepted_trade_off`, `client_decision`, `conditions`, `owner`, `review_event`, `progression_condition`, `invalidation_triggers`, `downstream_authority`.


The client narrative performs the seven consultancy functions in `FW_25`. Hold the full machine record transiently. Persist only the accepted decision, state axes, priority application, selected option, evaluation result and invalidation trigger in `RUN-MANIFEST.md`.

## Canonical output

**File:** `clients/[brand]/output/10-visual-strategy.md` (one file per client). *(Flat path for v1.x.)*

**Heading convention:** the client body uses the exact plain-language headings in `FW_26`. The **Visual Signature Label** remains a top-level field after its practical meaning has been explained. Runtime derivation maps each client section to `Layer 1`–`Layer 7`; no appendix is emitted by default.

```text
# Visual Strategy — [Brand Name]
<frontmatter: schema: m10-strategy · schema-version: 1.3 · brand · visual-signature>

## Creative idea
## Plain-language translation
## One-sentence designer brief
## Intended experience
## Why this follows from the Brand
## Visual characteristics
### [Characteristic]            intended feeling, brand-specific meaning, think, not-this
## Visual behaviours
## Creative tensions and anti-territories
## Creative freedom
## Practitioner handoff
## What is fixed, flexible and unresolved
## How the direction adapts across applications
## How concepts will be evaluated
## What still needs to be designed and approved
### Founder visual cues          imagery, motion, m05_source, applicability, reason
### Visual Catalyst record      reference_or_not_used, useful_quality, m01_m05_trace, rederived_decision
### Custom style specification  composition, colour, typography, imagery, motion, constraints, examples, application_rules
### Visual referenceability     decision, strategic_source, visible_behaviour, pass_fail
## How concepts will be briefed and evaluated
## What still needs to be designed and approved
```

---

## The six Resonance axes (canonical names)

| Axis (framework / Layer 3 canonical) | Note |
| --- | --- |
| Warm / Cool | |
| Restrained / Expressive | |
| **Spacious / Dense** | **Framework axis = `Spacious/Dense`.** The client-facing Visual Contract UI + outputs use **`Spacious/Full`** — a *deliberate* split ("Full" is the more choosable client word), recorded in `Products/visual-contract/.../module-10-mapping.md` and `system-summary.md`. **Do not "align" these** — read `Spacious/Dense` from the framework file; expect `Spacious/Full` in VC outputs. |
| Clean / Raw | |
| Calm / Energetic | |
| Focused / Layered | |

The Visual Contract's six pairs **are** Layer 3 — "not analogous to, the same axes" (`module-10-mapping.md`).

---

## The load-bearing fields

| What | Read-key | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Visual Signature Label** | top-level `**Visual Signature Label:**` | The 2–4 word owned descriptor every asset must express |
| **Layout and hierarchy** | client section | Containment, breathing and first-read behaviour |
| **Visual characteristics** | client section | Six commitments translated into feeling, Brand-specific meaning, Think and Not this |
| **Visual behaviours** | client section | Repeated reader experience and information jobs, without prescribed devices |
| **How the visual system should operate** | client section | Controlled vs Expressive state, explained in practical terms first |
| **Designer brief and production requirements** | client section | Principles, tokens/implementation boundary, RouteAuthorization, accessibility and required applications |

**For schema validation:** the Visual Signature Label, Layer 2, Layer 3, Layer 6, and Layer 7 **must be present** — 10B / `os-visual-asset-brief` cannot produce coherent output without a locked Layer 7 source and the operating model. Layers 1, 4, 5 are supporting (provenance + ranges); degrade gracefully but prefer them present. Layer 1 (inherited M05 conviction) is the spine. Founder visual cues require an applicability state; `not-applicable` is valid. A Visual Catalyst record may be `not-used`; when used it requires M01/M05 trace and a rederived decision. The custom style and material referenceability records must be executable and testable.

---

## Read-contract for skills

1. **Locate the practical client section.** The client body provides the usable decision; source and validation hashes in the manifest provide change control.
2. **Read the derived value from that section.** Reconstruct source quotations or internal mappings from the canonical authorities only when the task requires them.
3. **Respect the Operating Model.** `os-visual-asset-brief` must read Layer 6 first: **Controlled** → use only explicitly approved Layer 7 values verbatim; **Expressive** → respect principles + locked axes, interpreting free axes per-asset within the authorised Layer 4 behaviours and Layer 5 contextual guidance.
4. **Never confuse specification with finished design execution.** A Controlled, human-approved Module 10 route may lock exact palette, type, spacing and token values; an Expressive route preserves principles and authorised ranges. Skills may carry those approved values into briefs/specifications. Neither route produces a finished logo, composed page, complete identity system or other final visual artefact without separate production authority.
5. **Anchors guaranteed, the rest optional.** Signature + Layers 2/3/6/7 guaranteed; degrade gracefully on Layers 1/4/5.
6. **Version-check** the frontmatter `schema-version` against the skill's declared version.

**Cross-module read.** Layer 1 is inherited from M05; the authoritative conviction/brand fields read from M05 against `05-Strategy-Schema.md`. Each Layer 3 axis cites a quoted M05 word. Preserve that traceability as part of the framework’s intellectual property.

**Visual Contract outputs.** The Brief (designer-facing) + The Evaluation Companion (client-facing) are **canonical M10 deliverables**, generated by the visual-agent (`07-visual-agent.md`) from the locked Layer 3 positions, and live in the Visual Contract product format (`Products/visual-contract/`). They are a **sibling deliverable** to `10-visual-strategy.md` — `os-visual-asset-brief` *reads* Layer 3 but does not regenerate the VC outputs.

---

## Alias Map (current emission → canonical)

The client output uses plain-language headings. Runtime derivation uses `Layer N` tokens during generation; default outputs do not retain them.

**Read-rule (robust): match the `Layer N` token, not an exact heading string.** Find `Layer N` anywhere in the heading and read its Output / Step-2 block.

| Current heading | Read-key |
| --- | --- |
| Plain-language client heading | corresponding runtime `Layer N` |
| `**Visual Signature Label:** …` (or `## Visual Signature Label`) | Signature |
| Layer 3 axis table (`\| Axis \| Commitment \| Quoted M05 word \|`) | `Layer 3 → axis table` |
| `RUN-MANIFEST.md` source/state entry | change-control reference when the full canonical file is unavailable |

---

## Migration status

- [x] **Schema locked** (v1.0) — this document.
- [x] **Skills can read current output** — practical client sections are the stable read surface.
- [x] **Client emitter reformatted** — practical headings are primary; derivation is transient by default.
- [ ] **Roll-out complete after M10** — M05–M08 + M10 locked; M09 uses os-page-brief/os-page-copy. All five B-generators now have skills.

---

## Validation: visual-asset-brief (the new consumer) + the Langfell client gap

`.claude/skills/visual-asset-brief/SKILL.md` reads M10 against this schema:

| visual-asset-brief input | Read-key |
| --- | --- |
| Visual Signature Label | top-level Signature |
| Spatial Logic | `Layer 2 → Output` |
| Resonance Position (six axes + quoted M05 words) | `Layer 3 → Output` |
| Operating Model (lock vs interpret) | `Layer 6 → Output` |
| Output Artefact (Style System / Operating Constitution) + Image-Prompt Modifier Library + Derivation Chain | `Layer 7 → Output` |

**⚠ Langfell client gap (noted, not auto-fixed).** `clients/Langfell/output/10-visual-strategy.md` currently contains only **Layers 1, 2, 3, 6** — it predates the full seven-layer reconciliation (no Layer 4 ranges, Layer 5 narrowing, or Layer 7 artefact). The five **load-bearing** reads that exist (Signature, L2, L3, L6) resolve; **Layer 7 is absent**, so `visual-asset-brief` would hit its gate check ("Layer 7 not locked → return to 10-Prompt") for this client. Resolution: re-run M10 for the Langfell client to emit the full seven layers (it's the founder's own brand and the visual-agent is now on v3.0). Not a schema/skill defect — a client-file completeness gap, the M10 analogue of the M05 legacy-format finding.

---

## Version History

| Version | Date | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3 | 2026-08-21 | Made Canonical Strategy translation explicit: creative idea, tangible experience, characteristic interpretation, visual behaviours, anti-territories, creative freedom and practitioner handoff. |
| 1.2 | 2026-08-18 | Made conditional founder cues, rederived catalyst use, executable custom-style specification and visual-referenceability records native to the designer/production section. |
| 1.7 | 2026-08-17 | Required Practitioner Brief V3 metadata, common spine and complete Visual-specific middle for authorised concept and production handoffs. |
| 1.0 | 2026-06-01 | Initial M10 schema lock. **Layer-keyed** (not `10_NN`): seven-layer derivation chain; Visual Signature Label + Layers 2/3/6/7 as guaranteed load-bearing fields; six canonical Resonance axes with the deliberate `Spacious/Dense` (framework) vs `Spacious/Full` (client-facing VC) split preserved; Operating Model lock-vs-interpret read discipline; Visual Contract outputs documented as canonical sibling deliverables (read, not regenerated by the per-asset skill); `Layer N` token-match read-rule; validated against visual-asset-brief. Flagged the Langfell client's pre-reconciliation Layers-1/2/3/6-only file (Layer 7 absent → needs M10 re-run). Mirrors the schema family; completes the M05–M08+M10 roll-out. |

# Module 10: Visual Style Framework

**Langfell™**
_Layered Derivation System for Visual Identity_

---

## Purpose

The Visual Style Framework derives a brand's visual identity through seven layers, from conviction to execution in each medium. **It does not present a menu of named styles to select from.**

**Core principle:** Derivation, not selection. Every visual decision traces through the layers, each putting the previous one into practice. The 12 named styles later in this document provide **reference vocabulary**: labels used to communicate the result, never inputs to the derivation.

---

## The Layered Derivation Chain

Visual identity is derived through seven layers, each narrowing the previous:

```text
LAYER 1: CONVICTION
   (inherited from Module 05)
        |
        v
LAYER 2: SPATIAL LOGIC
   Focal point · Containment · Breathing
        |
        v
LAYER 3: RESONANCE POSITION
   Six binary pairs (property axes)
        |
        v
LAYER 4: DESIGN BEHAVIOUR TRANSLATION
   Translation engine — commitments to observable behaviour
        |
        v
LAYER 5: CONTEXT NARROWING
   Sector × Medium × Audience
        |
        v
LAYER 6: OPERATING MODEL
   Expressive (principles) vs Controlled (locked specs)
        |
        v
LAYER 7: OUTPUT ARTEFACTS
   Brand Style Guide / Operating Constitution / Style System
   + medium-specific derivatives (DESIGN.md, brand kit, etc.)
```

Each layer is necessary. Skipping any layer produces selection masquerading as derivation.

---

## Layer 1: Conviction (Module 05 Inheritance)

Layer 1 is **inherited, not derived**. It comes from Module 05 — the brand's Core Belief, Brand Personality, Values, Voice, Filter, and Positioning. Nothing in Module 10 modifies these. Everything in Module 10 derives from them.

**What Layer 1 provides:**

- The brand's belief — the conviction Module 10 makes visible
- The brand's personality — driving Layer 3's resonance position
- The brand's values — informing Layer 2's spatial logic
- The brand's voice — driving Layer 3's restraint axis
- The brand's filter — informing Layer 5's audience constraint

**Anchoring check:** Layer 1 must be genuinely anchored, not aspirational (see Gate 0 in `10-README.md`). A visual identity derived from aspirational Module 05 propagates the additive default at the most public layer of the business — the maximum-damage pattern named in `10-Philosophy.md`.

---

## Layer 2: Spatial Logic

Spatial Logic is the first visual translation of conviction. It defines **layout behaviour**, not specific values, through three properties:

### The Dot — Focal Logic

How the eye lands. How many focal points per composition. Where they sit relative to the frame. Whether they're anchored centrally, off-centre, or distributed.

**Derived from:** Module 05 Personality (assertive → strong central focal; quiet → off-centre or distributed) and Values (clarity → single focal; abundance → multiple focals).

### The Circle — Containment

What's inside the frame. Whether the brand uses tight containment (everything pulled toward the centre, controlled edges) or loose containment (elements permitted to break the grid, flow off the page).

**Derived from:** Module 05 Filter (tight Filter → tight containment; permissive Filter → loose containment) and Brand Strategy (premium → tight; democratic → loose).

### The Space Between — Breathing

The ratio between content and emptiness. Whether the brand operates at high information density or breathes generously. How much negative space functions as a design element in its own right.

**Derived from:** Module 05 Voice (restrained → generous breathing; expressive → dense) and Personality (quiet authority → generous; bold → dense).

**Output of Layer 2:** A short Spatial Logic statement, e.g., _"One focal point per composition. Tight containment. Generous breathing."_ This statement is medium-agnostic — it governs digital, print, packaging, and motion equally.

## Layer 3: Resonance Position

Layer 3 expresses the brand's emotional and perceptual posture through six binary pairs. The pairs derive from how audiences _perceive_ visual identities, rather than the techniques designers use to _produce_ them. They describe properties, not aesthetic categories.

### The Six Pairs

| Pair | Word A | Word B | What This Distinguishes |
| ---- | ------ | ------ | ----------------------- |
| 1 | Warm | Cool | Human/approachable vs precise/institutional |
| 2 | Spacious | Dense | Breathing room vs full/rich |
| 3 | Calm | Energetic | Still and quiet vs moving and loud |
| 4 | Restrained | Expressive | Held back vs bold statement |
| 5 | Clean | Raw | Polished and considered vs unpolished and honest |
| 6 | Focused | Layered | Single focal point vs multiple elements |

**Each pair marks a territory, not a point.** A brand sitting on the _Warm_ side isn't committing to any single shade of warmth — it's declaring direction. The Design Behaviour Translation at Layer 4 turns the direction into observable, testable practice without prematurely selecting a style.

### How Resonance Position Derives from Module 05

| Module 05 Output | Primary Resonance Axes |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| Personality | Warm/Cool, Restrained/Expressive |
| Values | Spacious/Dense, Clean/Raw |
| Voice | Calm/Energetic, Restrained/Expressive |
| Filter | Focused/Layered |
| Brand Strategy | All axes — final calibration |

**Output of Layer 3:** A six-axis resonance signature, e.g., _"Warm + Spacious + Calm + Restrained + Clean + Focused."_

### Why Pairs, Not Single Words

Each pair forces a directional commitment. _"This brand is warm"_ is a single direction; _"warm or cool — choose"_ is a forcing function. The binary commitment is what makes downstream interpretation possible. Spectrum language ("somewhat warm, kind of cool") cannot produce specifiable output.

The pairs are also the bridge to the parallel Langfell Visual Contract product, which uses the same six pairs as a free communication tool for non-designers briefing designers. Module 10 derives the position from conviction; the Visual Contract has the user choose by feel. Both produce the same six-axis resonance signature; the framework's contribution is the upstream derivation chain that anchors the position in conviction rather than preference.

---

## Layer 4: Design Behaviour Translation

Layer 4 translates each Layer 3 commitment into observable design behaviour. It explains what a practitioner should compose, prioritise, reduce, relate or test before choosing a style asset. It does not select typefaces, colours, grids, spacing values or final imagery.

For every commitment, record:

| Field | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Intent | Why this quality serves the strategy. |
| Behaviours | Observable choices in hierarchy, spacing, type, colour, imagery, interaction or material. |
| Verification | A context-appropriate inspection method. |
| Failure signals | Undershoot, overshoot or structural drift. |
| Freedom retained | Decisions the practitioner still owns. |

### Core behaviour rules

- **Warm:** introduce human presence, material or typographic character where it supports the message; do not equate warmth with warm colours, rounded corners or smiling people.
- **Spacious:** separate changes of thought, control density and allow consequential material room to land; do not prescribe a universal whitespace percentage.
- **Calm:** establish one clear entry point, limit competing emphasis and use motion only to clarify sequence or consequence.
- **Restrained:** make a few decisive moves, use accents purposefully and gain recognition through organising logic rather than ornament.
- **Clean:** make alignment, grouping, spacing and information states precise; clean must not mean sterile, generic or frictionless.
- **Focused:** give each principal surface one identifiable first-read element and visibly subordinate supporting material unless simultaneous attention is necessary and explained.

Typography must support sustained reading, decisive but non-theatrical hierarchy and distinct recommendation, evidence, qualification and metadata states. Colour must have a named job: recognition, focal direction, meaningful relationship or non-exclusive information state. Imagery must establish human presence, context, evidence, conceptual clarity, an intentional pause or recognition. Styling must not rescue an unresolved hierarchy, sequence or relationship.

### Conditional specification

Numeric values, token ranges and technical parameters may be created only after a concept route is selected and the operating model, medium, accessibility requirements and production fidelity authorise specification. They are project-specific implementation choices, not a universal meaning of a Resonance position.

**Output of Layer 4:** a commitment-by-commitment Design Behaviour Translation and selected design tests. Layer 5 narrows these behaviours for the actual sector, medium, audience and constraints.

---

## Layer 5: Context Narrowing

Layer 5 adapts the Layer 4 behaviours to _this brand's_ context. Examine the three narrowing inputs **independently**. A brand can be unusual on one and conventional on another; the record must show which condition changes each behaviour.

### Three Narrowing Sub-Inputs (Interrogated Separately)

**Sub-Input 5a — Sector context.** Trust-sensitive sectors may require more explicit evidence states, steadier hierarchy or additional accessibility constraints. _Ask: what does this brand's sector demand, and where does this brand intend to honour or deviate from that convention?_

**Sub-Input 5b — Medium.** Mobile, large-format print, packaging and motion each change how a behaviour can be expressed. _Ask: which media is this identity primarily expressed in, and what does each medium require?_

**Sub-Input 5c — Audience reading pattern.** Executive scanners may need a faster path into a Spacious direction; long-form readers may need more room for sustained reading. _Ask: how does this audience actually consume content, and what density and pace does that demand?_

Record the reasoning for each sub-input separately so a reviewer can trace each change in behaviour to its context.

### External Constraints (Permitted Non-Derived Inputs)

Layer 5 also accepts external constraints the brand must honour. Record these separately from inputs derived from conviction:

- **Accessibility floors** — AAA contrast ratios, minimum touch targets, font-size minimums. Non-negotiable regardless of resonance position.
- **Regulatory constraints** — sector-mandated colour/labelling rules (pharmaceutical, financial disclosure, food labelling, safety).
- **Platform constraints** — channel-specific aspect ratios, character limits, file-size ceilings, codec requirements.

These bound the authorised behaviour; they do not derive it. If an accessibility or legal requirement conflicts with an intended behaviour, the requirement wins and the record names the adjustment.

### The Narrowing Principle

```text
Contextual behaviour = Layer 4 behaviour, adapted by Sector (5a), Medium (5b), and Audience (5c) independently,
                     then bounded by any applicable External Constraints
```

Use judgement and record the source of each adaptation. Specific values belong only in an authorised later specification.

**Output of Layer 5:** contextual behaviour guidance for priority surfaces, accompanied by per-sub-input reasoning (5a, 5b, 5c) and an explicit External Constraints note.

## Layer 6: Operating Model

At Layer 6, the brand must explicitly choose an Operating Model. This choice determines what Layer 7 produces.

### Expressive vs Controlled

| | Expressive | Controlled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Examples | Teenage Engineering, Aesop, indie craft brands, founder-driven cult brands | Banks, law firms, insurance, healthcare, regulated SaaS, enterprise platforms |
| What stays constant | The animating principle — resonance, spatial logic, conviction | The specific specifications — typography, colour values, components, layout |
| What varies | Expression varies project-to-project, surface-to-surface | Expression is locked across touchpoints |
| Trust mechanism | Range itself signals authenticity ("they're alive, not on a template") | Consistency itself signals reliability ("they're solid, the same every time") |
| Output document | **Operating Constitution** | **Style System** |
| Decisions get made by | Reference to principles + fresh interpretation | Reference to fixed specs (lookup) |

### How to Decide

The choice is driven by four inputs:

- **Sector trust requirements** — regulated/trust-sensitive sectors → Controlled; creative sectors → either
- **Audience trust sensitivity** — high → Controlled; high creative-credibility → Expressive
- **Conviction posture** — _"we want to be recognisable above all"_ → Controlled; _"we want to feel alive and surprising"_ → Expressive
- **Distribution model** — mass-scale consumer brand → Controlled; founder-driven cult brand → Expressive

These usually converge. If they don't, sector trust requirements dominate.

**Output of Layer 6:** A single declaration — _"This brand operates Expressive"_ or _"This brand operates Controlled."_ Layer 7's output structure depends entirely on this choice.

### Hybrid Operation in Practice

The binary Controlled / Expressive declaration is a real choice the framework requires. It doesn't deny that real brands sometimes operate primarily one way with deliberate variance in the other — Aesop is mostly Controlled but ran Expressive editorial work; Patagonia is mostly Expressive but their product photography is tightly Controlled.

**The brand must declare one Primary Operating Mode at Layer 6.** If specific surfaces need the other mode, define them as **Secondary Mode Zones**. These are named exceptions with rules; the primary lock still holds.

Rules for Secondary Mode Zones:

1. **Named surfaces only.** A Secondary Mode Zone applies to specific touchpoints declared in advance — _"editorial content,"_ _"founder communications,"_ _"product photography,"_ _"seasonal campaigns."_ Not _"sometimes."_
2. **Bounded by the Visual Signature Label.** The Signature Label holds across both modes. A Controlled brand with an Expressive editorial zone still expresses the same Signature in both — the difference is whether values are locked or interpreted, not whether the conviction holds.
3. **The Primary Mode's Layer 7 artefact governs the boundary.** A Style System (Controlled-primary) with an Expressive editorial zone names what is locked even within the Expressive surface — typography family, palette frame, photographic conviction — and what is permitted to vary.
4. **Un-scoped drift between modes is the failure case.** A brand that's _sometimes_ Controlled and _sometimes_ Expressive without named zones is operating without a Layer 6 lock at all — the broken state the binary declaration exists to prevent.

The default is a brand with no Secondary Mode Zones. Hybrid operation is permitted within defined boundaries and rules; it does not remove the need for a Layer 6 decision.

**When Hybrid is the honest call:** if the four decision inputs above don't converge — for example, a creative-credibility audience (pulling Expressive) inside a trust-sensitive sector (pulling Controlled) — the answer is usually Controlled-primary with named Expressive Zones for the surfaces where creative credibility is the dominant trust mechanism. The reverse (Expressive-primary with Controlled Zones) is rarer but legitimate for founder-driven brands with regulated touchpoints (legal disclosures, packaging compliance, certifications).

### Worked Operating Model Cases

Use these as decision examples, not templates. The point is to show how the four inputs force the declaration.

| Case | Sector Trust | Audience Trust | Conviction Posture | Distribution | Declaration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Payroll compliance bureau** | High: payroll, pensions, HMRC exposure | High: owners need reliability more than novelty | "We remove risk quietly" | Repeatable B2B delivery | **Controlled.** Locked typography, colour, layout, and document templates carry the trust signal. Expressive range would read as instability. |
| **Founder-led furniture studio** | Low regulation; craft credibility matters | Buyers read material honesty and maker taste | "Furniture should show the hand that made it" | Small-batch, founder-led, portfolio-led sales | **Expressive.** The principle stays constant, but each collection can carry a slightly different expression. Locking every surface would flatten the maker signal. |
| **B2B workflow consultancy** | Moderate: operational advice must feel serious | Founders want truth without theatricality | "The workflow lies before the team fails" | Website, diagnostic reports, workshops | **Controlled.** The diagnostic posture depends on repeatable evidence presentation. Diagrams, annotations, and report layouts need a locked system. |
| **Design-led fertility clinic** | High: healthcare trust, consent, patient safety | Also high creative sensitivity: patients want warmth, not institutionality | "Clinical care can feel human without becoming vague" | Clinic environment, website, patient documents, founder essays | **Controlled-primary with Expressive Zones.** Clinical journey, consent, pricing, and treatment pages stay Controlled. Founder essays, waiting-room editorial, and community events become named Expressive Zones bounded by the same Visual Signature Label. |

The Hybrid case retains one Primary Operating Mode and names the exceptions: the surfaces allowed to interpret the conviction rather than repeat the specification.

## Layer 7: Output Artefacts

Layer 7 produces the framework's deliverables. The artefact structure depends on the Layer 6 declaration. Every Layer 7 artefact must separate **Principles**, **Tokens**, and **Implementation**, and include **accessibility** and **RouteAuthorization** notes.

### Required at the Top of Every Layer 7 Artefact: The Visual Signature Label

Before the specification details (Controlled) or principles (Expressive), every Layer 7 artefact opens with a **Visual Signature Label** — a short proprietary descriptor (typically 2–4 words) that names the visual position the chain derived. Examples: _Restrained Confidence_, _Quiet Architecture_, _Warm Precision_, _Disciplined Play_.

The Signature Label is **owned by the brand**, distinct from the 12 named styles. It derives from the brand's Layer 1 conviction, Layer 3 resonance position and Layer 5 context. Builders, clients and downstream collaborators use it to discuss the visual identity in the brand's own terms, without importing a named style's cultural baggage.

A builder who has paid for a brand process needs a position they can **name** and explain. _"Our visual signature is Restrained Confidence — here's what that means and what it doesn't"_ gives them that, even when no named style fits.

Authoring rules:

- 2–4 words, no longer
- Drawn from the brand's own conviction vocabulary (Module 01 Natural Language Bank) where possible
- Names the **position**, not the **mood** ("Restrained Confidence" not "Calm and Trustworthy")
- Cannot be the same as one of the 12 named styles, and must not be a synonym ("Quiet Minimalism" is just Minimalism)
- Must be traceable: the artefact lists which Layer 3 axis positions and which Layer 1 conviction inputs produced it

### If Controlled → Style System

A locked specification artefact containing:

- **Visual Signature Label** (required — see above)
- **Principles section** — why each visual choice exists, linked to M05 anchors
- **Tokens** — named, platform-agnostic values (colour, type scale, spacing, radius, motion)
- **Implementation examples** — web, print, motion, packaging references to tokens without redefining them
- **Brand Style Guide** (medium-agnostic art direction — the source of truth)
- **DESIGN.md** (digital design system with locked values, consuming the tokens)
- **Print spec sheet** (CMYK, paper stock, finish, structural rules)
- **Brand kit** (Canva or similar, populated with locked values)
- **Design tokens** (JSON file consumable by build systems)
- **Image-prompt modifier library** (locked phrase set for AI image generation)
- **Logo and lockup specifications**
- **Component library** (buttons, cards, forms — locked styling, referencing tokens)
- **Accessibility notes** — minimum contrast, readable type sizes, focus states, reduced-motion preference
- **RouteAuthorization field** — copied from M04

Every value is locked, and every touchpoint references the same specs to keep the brand's expression consistent across contexts.

### If Expressive → Operating Constitution

A principles artefact containing:

- **Visual Signature Label** (required — see above)
- **Principles section** — why each visual choice exists, linked to M05 anchors
- **Tokens** — named, platform-agnostic values where the brand does lock a value (e.g. primary typeface, signature colour), with free axes left as ranges
- **Implementation examples** — web, print, motion, packaging references to tokens without redefining them
- **Conviction-anchored visual character statement** (philosophical centre)
- **Spatial logic principles** (focal/containment/breathing — operationalised but not numeric)
- **Resonance position** with _examples_ of acceptable expression range across multiple touchpoints
- **Decision questions** for new touchpoints (_"what does our conviction demand here?"_)
- **Example renderings** showing the range — three to five distinct expressions, all coherent
- **Image-prompt modifier library** (less restrictive than Controlled version — emphasises the conviction, leaves room for context)
- **Boundary statements** (what the brand never does)
- **Accessibility notes** — minimum contrast, readable type sizes, focus states, reduced-motion preference
- **RouteAuthorization field** — copied from M04

For each new touchpoint, ask: _"Given our principles, how should this particular expression go?"_ Expression varies across contexts; shared principles keep it coherent.

### Common Layer 7 Outputs (Both Operating Models)

Regardless of operating model, every Layer 7 artefact includes:

- **Image-prompt modifier library** — brand-specific phrases for AI image generation, derived from Layer 4 behaviours
- **Photography direction** (mood, subject, treatment, what to avoid)
- **Application examples across mediums**
- **Do/Don't usage rules**
- **Source document linkage** — every downstream artefact (DESIGN.md, brand kit, etc.) cites the Layer 7 source
- **Principles / Tokens / Implementation separation** — principles explain why, tokens are named values, implementation examples reference tokens
- **Accessibility notes** — contrast, readable type sizes, focus states, reduced-motion preference
- **RouteAuthorization field** — copied from M04

### Handoff to the Design Industry

The Layer 7 artefact (Style System or Operating Constitution) is the framework's canonical source. Designers, agencies, and in-house design teams don't work from artefacts with these names — they work from brand guidelines, design systems, design tokens, Figma libraries, and creative briefs. Layer 7 sits upstream of all of those; it doesn't replace any of them.

The practitioner uses Layer 7 to brief the conventional deliverable, which the designer then produces. Both documents exist and serve different audiences.

| Layer 7 Source (Langfell-internal) | Conventional Deliverable (industry-facing) | Who Builds It |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Style System (Controlled) | **Brand Guidelines** document — logo, typography, colour, voice, usage rules | Designer or agency, from the Style System brief |
| Style System (Controlled) | **Design System** — Figma library, component specs, design tokens (JSON), CSS variables | Designer / design engineer, from the Style System's locked numeric values |
| Operating Constitution (Expressive) | **Creative Brief** + **Principles Doc** — articulates the conviction and the range, with three to five reference renderings | Practitioner or strategist, with designer review |
| Operating Constitution (Expressive) | **Reference Library** — curated examples of acceptable expression, with annotations on what makes each one coherent | Designer or art director, with practitioner approval |
| Either | **Image-prompt modifier library** | Practitioner — already produced as part of Layer 7 |
| Either | **Photography brief** for shoots | Practitioner or art director, from Layer 7 photography direction |

In most engagements, the practitioner **adapts Layer 7 into a brief for the designer**. It serves the same purpose as a creative director's internal strategy document: the source for the production brief sent to the studio.

What the designer needs to know about Layer 7:

- It is the canonical source — every conventional deliverable derives from it
- It contains the Visual Signature Label, which the designer should treat as the brand's owned position (not as one of the 12 named styles)
- The approved behaviours, contextual constraints and later authorised specifications are non-negotiable downstream — the designer's role is to express them across mediums, not to relitigate them
- Changes to the visual identity require Layer 7 to be amended first, not the designer's deliverable

What the practitioner needs to deliver to a designer:

- The Visual Signature Label and a short paragraph on what it means
- The Layer 7 locked values (Controlled) or principles + range examples (Expressive)
- The image-prompt modifier library
- The photography direction
- The Do/Don't usage rules
- The application examples across mediums
- A conventional creative brief that translates the above into the deliverable's format

A designer or agency builds the brand guidelines from the practitioner's brief. Layer 7 supplies the source from which those deliverables derive.

## Chain Re-Entry

Real visual identity work iterates. The rule is simple: identify the first broken layer, then re-run from that layer forward. Do not patch the visible output while leaving the broken layer untouched.

### How to Find the Broken Layer

| Symptom in live use | First layer to inspect | Typical cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The identity feels polished but false | Layer 1 / Module 05 | Brand identity was aspirational or has changed |
| People feel _something_, but not the intended conviction | Layer 3 | Resonance Position expressed the wrong emotional posture |
| Values are right in principle but inconsistent in execution | Layer 4 | Commitments were not translated into usable behaviours and verification |
| Website works but social, print, or product surfaces break | Layer 5 | Sector/medium/audience narrowing was incomplete |
| Designers keep asking whether to follow rules or interpret principles | Layer 6 | Operating Model was implicit or Secondary Mode Zones were not scoped |
| One new campaign sits outside the identity but the core system still works | Layer 7 | Layer 7 needs an amendment, not a full rebrand |

### Cost of Change

| First broken layer | Cost level | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layer 1 / Module 05 | Rebrand-level | Re-lock Module 05 and re-run Module 10 from the start. Public explanation may be needed. |
| Layer 3 | High | Rebuild resonance, behaviour translation, operating model, and Layer 7. Existing visual assets may need replacement. |
| Layer 4 | Medium | Rework behaviours and downstream briefs. Public identity may stay recognisable, but execution rules change. |
| Layer 5 | Low to medium | Recalibrate affected media or audience contexts. Usually a touchpoint correction. |
| Layer 6 | Medium | Re-issue the Layer 7 artefact as Style System or Operating Constitution, and brief downstream teams again. |
| Layer 7 | Low | Amend the source artefact and regenerate affected 10B outputs. No public change is required unless shipped assets are already live. |

### Communication Rule

Name the change at the same depth as the break. Do not tell a team _"we're refreshing the visuals"_ if the truth is _"our Module 05 anchor was aspirational."_ Do not tell the market _"we've rebranded"_ if the truth is only _"we tightened our social templates."_ Accurate naming prevents defensive explanation and keeps the system honest.

Iteration is expected. Skipping is not.
